verses.1:1: Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim Zophim, from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
verses.1:2: And he had two wives: the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the second was Peninnah. Peninnah had children, yet Hannah had no children.
verses.1:3: Now this man went up from his city year by year to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of hosts in Shiloh. And there the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to the LORD.
verses.1:4: And whenever the day came that Elkanah offered sacrifice, he would give portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters.
verses.1:5: Yet to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved Hannah, though the LORD had closed her womb.
verses.1:6: And her rival also provoked her bitterly to vex her, because the LORD had shut up her womb.
verses.1:7: So he did year after year: as often as she went up to the house of the LORD, thus she provoked her; therefore she wept and would not eat.
verses.1:8: Then Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
verses.1:9: So Hannah rose up after eating in Shiloh, and after drinking. Now Eli the priest was sitting upon the seat by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.
verses.1:10: And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly.
verses.1:11: Then she vowed a vow and said, "O LORD of hosts, if You will indeed look upon the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, and not forget Your maidservant, and will give to Your maidservant a male child, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall come upon his head."
verses.1:12: And it came to pass, as she continued praying before the LORD, that Eli watched her mouth.
verses.1:13: Now Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved, yet her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli thought her to be drunk.
verses.1:14: So Eli said to her, "How long will you be drunk? Put your wine away from you!"
verses.1:15: And Hannah answered and said, "No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit. I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, yet I have poured out my soul before the LORD.
verses.1:16: Do not regard your maidservant as a worthless woman, for out of the abundance of my complaint and my grief I have spoken until now."
verses.1:17: Then Eli answered and said, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant your petition which you have asked of Him."
verses.1:18: And she said, "Let your handmaid find favor in your sight." So the woman went her way and ate, and her countenance was no longer downcast.
verses.1:19: Then they rose early in the morning and worshiped before the LORD, and returned and came to their house in Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her.
verses.1:20: And it came to pass in the course of time that Hannah conceived and bore a son; and she called his name Samuel, saying, "Because I have asked for him from the LORD."
verses.1:21: Now the man Elkanah and all his household went up to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and his vow.
verses.1:22: Yet Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, "Not until the child is weaned; then I will bring him, that he may appear before the LORD and abide there forever."
verses.1:23: So Elkanah her husband said to her, "Do what is good in your eyes; remain until you have weaned him. Only may the LORD establish His word." Thus the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him.
verses.1:24: And when she had weaned him, she brought him up with her, with three bulls, and one ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of the LORD in Shiloh; and the child was yet young.
verses.1:25: Then they slaughtered the bull, and brought the child to Eli.
verses.1:26: And she said, "Oh, my lord! As your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who stood by you here, praying to the LORD.
verses.1:27: For this child I prayed, and the LORD has granted me my petition which I asked of Him.
verses.1:28: Therefore I also have lent him to the LORD; all the days that he lives he is lent to the LORD." And he worshiped the LORD there.
verses.2:1: And Hannah prayed and said, "My heart exults in the LORD; my horn is exalted in the LORD. My mouth is opened wide over my enemies, because I rejoice in Your salvation.
verses.2:2: There is none holy like the LORD, for there is none besides You, nor is there any rock like our God.
verses.2:3: Do not speak any longer so very proudly; let no arrogance come forth from your mouth, for the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by Him actions are weighed.
verses.2:4: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and those who stumbled are girded with strength.
verses.2:5: Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread, and the hungry have ceased to hunger; even the barren woman has borne seven, and she who had many sons has languished.
verses.2:6: The LORD puts to death and makes alive; He brings down to Sheol and brings up.
verses.2:7: The LORD makes poor and makes rich; He brings low and also lifts up.
verses.2:8: He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap, to seat them with nobles and make them inherit a throne of glory. For the pillars of the earth belong to the LORD, and He has set the world upon them.
verses.2:9: He will guard the feet of His saints, yet the wicked shall be silenced in darkness; for by strength no man shall prevail.
verses.2:10: The adversaries of the LORD shall be shattered; against them He shall thunder in the heavens. The LORD shall judge the ends of the earth; He shall give strength to His king, and exalt the horn of His anointed."
verses.2:11: Then Elkanah went to Ramah to his house; and the boy ministered to the LORD before Eli the priest.
verses.2:12: Now the sons of Eli were worthless men; they did not know the LORD.
verses.2:13: And the custom of the priests with the people was this: when any man offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fleshhook in his hand.
verses.2:14: And he would thrust it into the pan, or kettle, or cauldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up, the priest took for himself. Thus they did to all Israel who came there to Shiloh.
verses.2:15: Moreover, before they burned the fat, the priest's servant would come and say to the man who sacrificed, "Give meat to roast for the priest, for he will not accept boiled meat from you, but raw."
verses.2:16: And if the man said to him, "Let them surely burn the fat first, and then take for yourself as much as your soul desires," then he would answer, "No, for you shall give it now; and if not, I will take it by force."
verses.2:17: Therefore the sin of the young men was exceedingly great before the LORD, for the men despised the offering of the LORD.
verses.2:18: Now Samuel ministered before the LORD, a boy girded with a linen ephod.
verses.2:19: And his mother would make him a little robe and bring it up to him year by year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
verses.2:20: And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, and say, "May the LORD give you offspring from this woman in place of the loan that was lent to the LORD." Then they would go back to his home.
verses.2:21: And indeed the LORD visited Hannah, so that she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. Meanwhile the boy Samuel grew before the LORD.
verses.2:22: Now Eli was very old; and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they lay with the women who served at the doorway of the tent of meeting.
verses.2:23: So he said to them, "Why do you do such things as these? For I hear of your evil doings from all these people.
verses.2:24: No, my sons! For it is not a good report that I hear; you cause the LORD's people to transgress.
verses.2:25: If one man sins against another, God will mediate for him; yet if a man sins against the LORD, who shall intercede for him?" Nevertheless they did not heed the voice of their father, because the LORD desired to put them to death.
verses.2:26: And the boy Samuel continued to grow in stature, and in favor both with the LORD and also with men.
verses.2:27: Then a man of God came to Eli and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: Did I not plainly reveal Myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt, belonging to Pharaoh's house?
verses.2:28: And did I not choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be My priest, to go up to My altar, to burn incense, and to wear an ephod before Me? And I gave to the house of your father all the fire offerings of the children of Israel.
verses.2:29: Why then do you kick at My sacrifice and at My offering which I have commanded in My habitation, and honor your sons above Me, to make yourselves fat with the choicest of all the offerings of Israel My people?
verses.2:30: Therefore the LORD, the God of Israel, declares: I indeed said that your house and the house of your father should walk before Me forever; yet now the LORD declares: Far be it from Me! For those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed.
verses.2:31: Behold, the days are coming when I will cut off your arm and the arm of your father's house, so that there shall not be an old man in your house.
verses.2:32: And you shall behold distress in the habitation, amid all the good that He will bestow upon Israel; and there shall never be an old man in your house for all time.
verses.2:33: Yet the man of yours whom I do not cut off from My altar shall remain to consume your eyes and to grieve your soul; and all the increase of your house shall die in the prime of manhood.
verses.2:34: And this shall be the sign to you that shall come upon your two sons, upon Hophni and Phinehas: in one day both of them shall die.
verses.2:35: Then I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest who shall do according to what is in My heart and in My soul; and I will build for him a sure house, and he shall walk before My anointed forever.
verses.2:36: And it shall come to pass that everyone who is left in your house shall come to bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and shall say, 'Please assign me to one of the priestly offices, that I may eat a morsel of bread.'"
verses.3:1: Now the lad Samuel was ministering to the LORD before Eli. And the word of the LORD was rare in those days; there was no widespread vision.
verses.3:2: And it came to pass in that day, while Eli was lying down in his place, and his eyes had begun to grow dim so that he could not see,
verses.3:3: and the lamp of God had not yet gone out, while Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was,
verses.3:4: that the LORD called to Samuel. And he said, "Here I am!"
verses.3:5: So he ran to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." And he said, "I did not call; go back and lie down." So he went and lay down.
verses.3:6: Then the LORD called yet again, "Samuel!" So Samuel arose and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." And he said, "I did not call, my son; go back and lie down."
verses.3:7: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, nor had the word of the LORD yet been revealed to him.
verses.3:8: And the LORD called Samuel again a third time. So he arose and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." Then Eli perceived that the LORD was calling the lad.
verses.3:9: Therefore Eli said to Samuel, "Go, lie down; and it shall be, if He calls to you, that you shall say, 'Speak, LORD, for Your servant hears.'" So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
verses.3:10: Then the LORD came and stood, and called as at the other times, "Samuel! Samuel!" And Samuel said, "Speak, for Your servant hears."
verses.3:11: Then the LORD said to Samuel, "Behold, I am about to do a thing in Israel at which both ears of everyone who hears it shall tingle.
verses.3:12: In that day I will carry out against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from beginning to end.
verses.3:13: For I have declared to him that I will judge his house forever for the iniquity which he knew, because his sons were bringing a curse upon themselves, and he did not restrain them.
verses.3:14: Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of the house of Eli shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or offering forever."
verses.3:15: So Samuel lay down until morning, and he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. And Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.
verses.3:16: Then Eli called Samuel and said, "Samuel, my son!" And he answered, "Here I am."
verses.3:17: And he said, "What is the word that He spoke to you? Please do not conceal it from me. May God do so to you, and more also, if you conceal anything from me of all the words that He spoke to you."
verses.3:18: Then Samuel told him all the words, and concealed nothing from him. And he said, "It is the LORD; let Him do what is good in His sight."
verses.3:19: So Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground.
verses.3:20: And all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was established as a prophet of the LORD.
verses.3:21: And the LORD appeared again at Shiloh, for the LORD revealed Himself to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of the LORD.
verses.4:1: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out to meet the Philistines in battle, and encamped beside Ebenezer; and the Philistines encamped at Aphek.
verses.4:2: And the Philistines drew up in battle array against Israel. When the battle spread, Israel was defeated before the Philistines, who struck down about four thousand men in the battle line on the field.
verses.4:3: And when the people came into the camp, the elders of Israel said, "Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let us bring to ourselves the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, that it may come into our midst and save us from the hand of our enemies."
verses.4:4: So the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned above the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
verses.4:5: And it came to pass, when the ark of the covenant of the LORD entered the camp, that all Israel shouted with a mighty shout, so that the earth resounded.
verses.4:6: Now when the Philistines heard the sound of the shout, they said, "What is the sound of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews?" Then they learned that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.
verses.4:7: So the Philistines were afraid, for they said, "God has come into the camp!" And they said, "Woe to us! For nothing like this has happened before.
verses.4:8: Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with every plague in the wilderness.
verses.4:9: Take courage and be men, O Philistines, lest you serve the Hebrews, as they have served you. Be men, and fight!"
verses.4:10: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and every man fled to his tent. The slaughter was exceedingly great, for thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.
verses.4:11: Also the ark of God was captured, and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
verses.4:12: Then a man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and reached Shiloh that same day, with his garments torn and earth upon his head.
verses.4:13: Now when he arrived, behold, Eli was sitting on his seat beside the road, watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God. And when the man came into the city to report it, all the city cried out.
verses.4:14: When Eli heard the sound of the outcry, he said, "What is the sound of this tumult?" And the man hastened and came and told Eli.
verses.4:15: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were fixed so that he could not see.
verses.4:16: And the man said to Eli, "I am he who has come from the battle line; I fled from the battle line today." And he said, "What has happened, my son?"
verses.4:17: So the messenger answered and said, "Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has also been a great slaughter among the people. Furthermore, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been captured."
verses.4:18: And it came to pass, when he made mention of the ark of God, that Eli fell backward off the seat beside the gate; and his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.
verses.4:19: Now his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was with child, about to give birth; and when she heard the report that the ark of God had been captured, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth, for her labor pains came upon her.
verses.4:20: And about the time of her death, the women who stood by her said, "Do not fear, for you have borne a son." But she did not answer, nor did she take it to heart.
verses.4:21: Then she named the child Ichabod, saying, "The glory has departed from Israel!" because the ark of God had been captured, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
verses.4:22: And she said, "The glory has departed from Israel, for the ark of God has been captured."
verses.5:1: Now the Philistines took the ark of God and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
verses.5:2: And the Philistines took the ark of God and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it beside Dagon.
verses.5:3: And when the people of Ashdod arose early the next day, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and restored him to his place.
verses.5:4: And when they arose early the next morning, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD; and the head of Dagon and both palms of his hands lay severed upon the threshold; only the trunk of Dagon was left to him.
verses.5:5: Therefore neither the priests of Dagon nor any who enter the house of Dagon tread upon the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod to this day.
verses.5:6: Now the hand of the LORD was heavy upon the people of Ashdod, and He devastated them and struck them with tumors, both Ashdod and its territories.
verses.5:7: And when the men of Ashdod saw how it was, they said, "The ark of the God of Israel must not remain with us, for His hand is severe upon us and upon Dagon our god."
verses.5:8: Therefore they sent and gathered all the lords of the Philistines to themselves, and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" And they answered, "Let the ark of the God of Israel be carried around to Gath." So they carried the ark of the God of Israel there.
verses.5:9: And it came to pass, after they had carried it there, that the hand of the LORD was against the city with an exceedingly great panic; and He struck the men of the city, from the smallest to the greatest, and tumors broke out upon them.
verses.5:10: Therefore they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it came to pass, as the ark of God entered Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out, saying, "They have brought the ark of the God of Israel around to us, to slay us and our people!"
verses.5:11: So they sent and gathered all the lords of the Philistines, and said, "Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it return to its own place, lest it slay us and our people." For there was a deadly panic throughout all the city; the hand of God was exceedingly heavy there.
verses.5:12: And the men who did not die were struck with tumors, and the cry of the city went up to heaven.
verses.6:1: Now the ark of the LORD was in the territory of the Philistines seven months.
verses.6:2: And the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, "What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place."
verses.6:3: And they said, "If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it empty; rather, by all means return a guilt offering to Him. Then you shall be healed, and it will be made known to you why His hand has not turned away from you."
verses.6:4: Then they said, "What is the guilt offering that we shall return to Him?" And they answered, "According to the number of the lords of the Philistines: five golden tumors and five golden mice, for one plague was upon all of them and upon your lords.
verses.6:5: Therefore you shall make likenesses of your tumors and likenesses of your mice that are ravaging the land, and you shall give glory to the God of Israel; perhaps He will lighten His hand from you, from your gods, and from your land.
verses.6:6: Why then should you harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When He had dealt severely with them, did they not let them go, and they departed?
verses.6:7: Now therefore, take and make one new cart, and take two milk cows on which no yoke has ever come; and hitch the cows to the cart, and take their calves back home, away from following them.
verses.6:8: Then take the ark of the LORD and set it on the cart, and put the articles of gold which you are returning to Him as a guilt offering in a chest beside it; then send it away, and let it go.
verses.6:9: And watch: if it goes up by the way of its own border to Beth Shemesh, then He has done us this great evil. But if not, then we shall know that it was not His hand that struck us; it happened to us by chance."
verses.6:10: So the men did this: they took two milk cows and hitched them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home.
verses.6:11: And they set the ark of the LORD on the cart, and the chest with the golden mice and the likenesses of their tumors.
verses.6:12: Then the cows went straight along the way toward Beth Shemesh; they walked along the one highway, lowing as they went, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. And the lords of the Philistines walked after them to the border of Beth Shemesh.
verses.6:13: Now the people of Beth Shemesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.
verses.6:14: Then the cart came into the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh and stood still there, where a large stone was. And they split the wood of the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.6:15: And the Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the chest that was with it, in which were the articles of gold, and set them upon the large stone. And the men of Beth Shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices that day to the LORD.
verses.6:16: And when the five lords of the Philistines saw it, they returned to Ekron the same day.
verses.6:17: Now these are the golden tumors which the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to the LORD: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, and one for Ekron;
verses.6:18: and the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, from fortified city to unwalled village, even as far as Great Abel, on which they set down the ark of the LORD, which remains to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh.
verses.6:19: And He struck the men of Beth Shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the LORD; He struck among the people seventy men, fifty thousand men. And the people mourned because the LORD had struck the people with a great slaughter.
verses.6:20: And the men of Beth Shemesh said, "Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? And to whom shall He go up from us?"
verses.6:21: So they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath Jearim, saying, "The Philistines have brought back the ark of the LORD; come down and take it up to you."
verses.7:1: Then the men of Kiriath Jearim came and brought up the ark of the LORD, and carried it into the house of Abinadab on the hill, and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the LORD.
verses.7:2: And it came to pass, from the day that the ark remained in Kiriath Jearim, that the time was long, for it was twenty years; and all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.
verses.7:3: Then Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, "If you return to the LORD with all your hearts, put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct your hearts to the LORD and serve Him alone; and He will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.7:4: So the children of Israel put away the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served the LORD alone.
verses.7:5: And Samuel said, "Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you."
verses.7:6: So they gathered together at Mizpah, drew water, and poured it out before the LORD. And they fasted on that day, and said there, "We have sinned against the LORD." And Samuel judged the children of Israel at Mizpah.
verses.7:7: Now when the Philistines heard that the children of Israel had gathered together at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the children of Israel heard of it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
verses.7:8: So the children of Israel said to Samuel, "Do not cease to cry out to the LORD our God for us, that He may save us from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.7:9: And Samuel took a nursing lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. Then Samuel cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.
verses.7:10: Now as Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle against Israel. But the LORD thundered with a mighty thunder upon the Philistines that day and threw them into confusion, and they were defeated before Israel.
verses.7:11: And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them down as far as below Beth Car.
verses.7:12: Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, "Thus far the LORD has helped us."
verses.7:13: So the Philistines were subdued, and they did not come anymore into the territory of Israel. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
verses.7:14: Then the cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron to Gath; and Israel delivered their territory from the hand of the Philistines. Also there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
verses.7:15: And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
verses.7:16: He went from year to year on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and judged Israel in all those places.
verses.7:17: Then his return was to Ramah, for his house was there; and there he judged Israel, and there he built an altar to the LORD.
verses.8:1: Now it came to pass when Samuel was old that he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
verses.8:2: The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah; they were judges in Beersheba.
verses.8:3: Yet his sons did not walk in his ways; they turned aside after dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.
verses.8:4: Then all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah,
verses.8:5: and said to him, "Behold, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint for us a king to judge us, like all the nations."
verses.8:6: But the matter was displeasing in the eyes of Samuel when they said, "Give us a king to judge us." So Samuel prayed to the LORD.
verses.8:7: And the LORD said to Samuel, "Heed the voice of the people in all that they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them.
verses.8:8: According to all the deeds which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even to this day—forsaking Me and serving other gods—so they are doing to you also.
verses.8:9: Now therefore, heed their voice; yet you shall solemnly warn them and declare to them the practice of the king who shall reign over them."
verses.8:10: So Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who asked him for a king.
verses.8:11: And he said, "This shall be the practice of the king who shall reign over you: he will take your sons and appoint them for himself, for his chariots and to be his horsemen, and some will run before his chariots.
verses.8:12: He will appoint for himself commanders over thousands and commanders over fifties, and set some to plow his ground and to reap his harvest, and to make his weapons of war and the equipment for his chariots.
verses.8:13: He will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
verses.8:14: And he will take the best of your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves, and give them to his servants.
verses.8:15: He will take a tenth of your grain and your vineyards, and give it to his officers and to his servants.
verses.8:16: And he will take your male servants, your female servants, your finest young men, and your donkeys, and put them to his work.
verses.8:17: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves shall become his servants.
verses.8:18: And you will cry out in that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, and the LORD will not answer you in that day."
verses.8:19: Nevertheless the people refused to heed the voice of Samuel; and they said, "No, but there shall be a king over us,
verses.8:20: that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us and go out before us and fight our battles."
verses.8:21: And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and repeated them in the hearing of the LORD.
verses.8:22: So the LORD said to Samuel, "Heed their voice, and make a king for them." And Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Go, every man to his city."
verses.9:1: Now there was a man of Benjamin whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a Benjamite, a mighty man of valor.
verses.9:2: And he had a son whose name was Saul, a choice young man and handsome; there was not a man among the children of Israel more handsome than he. From his shoulders upward he was taller than all the people.
verses.9:3: Now the donkeys of Kish, Saul's father, were lost. And Kish said to his son Saul, "Please take one of the young servants with you, and arise, go search for the donkeys."
verses.9:4: So he passed through the hill country of Ephraim and passed through the land of Shalishah, but they did not find them. Then they passed through the land of Shaalim, and they were not there. Then he passed through the land of the Benjamites, yet they did not find them.
verses.9:5: When they had come to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant who was with him, "Come, let us return, lest my father cease caring about the donkeys and become anxious for us."
verses.9:6: And he said to him, "Behold, now, there is a man of God in this city, and the man is held in honor; all that he speaks surely comes to pass. Now let us go there; perhaps he will tell us concerning our journey on which we have come."
verses.9:7: Then Saul said to his servant, "Behold, if we go, what shall we bring the man? For the bread is gone from our vessels, and there is no gift to bring to the man of God. What do we have?"
verses.9:8: And the servant answered Saul again and said, "Behold, there is found in my hand a fourth of a shekel of silver. I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way."
verses.9:9: Formerly in Israel, thus a man would say when he went to inquire of God, "Come, let us go to the seer," for he who is called a prophet today was formerly called a seer.
verses.9:10: Then Saul said to his servant, "Your word is good; come, let us go." So they went to the city where the man of God was.
verses.9:11: As they were going up the ascent to the city, they encountered young women going out to draw water, and they said to them, "Is the seer in this place?"
verses.9:12: And they answered them and said, "He is; behold, he is right ahead of you. Make haste now, for today he has come to the city, because the people have a sacrifice today on the high place.
verses.9:13: As soon as you enter the city, you will surely find him before he goes up to the high place to eat; for the people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice, and afterward those who are invited will eat. Now therefore go up, for about this time you will find him."
verses.9:14: So they went up to the city. As they were coming into the midst of the city, behold, Samuel was coming out toward them to go up to the high place.
verses.9:15: Now the LORD had revealed in Samuel's ear one day before Saul came, saying,
verses.9:16: "Tomorrow about this time I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as prince over My people Israel; and he shall save My people from the hand of the Philistines. For I have looked upon My people, because their cry has come to Me."
verses.9:17: And when Samuel saw Saul, the LORD answered him, "Behold the man of whom I spoke to you! This one shall govern My people."
verses.9:18: Then Saul drew near to Samuel in the midst of the gate and said, "Please tell me, where is the house of the seer?"
verses.9:19: And Samuel answered Saul and said, "I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, for you shall eat with me today; and in the morning I will let you go and will declare to you all that is in your heart.
verses.9:20: And as for your donkeys that were lost three days ago, do not set your heart upon them, for they have been found. And for whom is all that is desirable in Israel? Is it not for you and for all your father's house?"
verses.9:21: And Saul answered and said, "Am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? Why then have you spoken to me after this manner?"
verses.9:22: Then Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the hall, and gave them a place at the head of those who were invited, who were about thirty men.
verses.9:23: And Samuel said to the cook, "Bring the portion which I gave you, of which I said to you, 'Set it apart with you.'"
verses.9:24: So the cook lifted up the thigh with what was upon it and set it before Saul. And he said, "Behold what was reserved; it is set before you. Eat, for it has been kept for you until the appointed time, since I said, 'I have invited the people.'" So Saul ate with Samuel on that day.
verses.9:25: And when they had come down from the high place into the city, he spoke with Saul upon the roof.
verses.9:26: And they arose early; and it came to pass about the breaking of the dawn that Samuel called to Saul up to the roof, saying, "Arise, that I may send you on your way." So Saul arose, and both of them went outside, he and Samuel.
verses.9:27: As they were going down to the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell the servant to pass on ahead of us." And he passed on. "But as for you, stand still now, that I may make you hear the word of God."
verses.10:1: Then Samuel took a flask of oil and poured it upon his head, and kissed him and said, "Has not the LORD anointed you as prince over His inheritance?
verses.10:2: When you have departed from me today, you will find two men by Rachel's tomb in the territory of Benjamin at Zelzah; and they will say to you, 'The donkeys which you went to search for have been found. And behold, your father has left off caring about the donkeys and is anxious for you, saying, "What shall I do for my son?"'
verses.10:3: Then you shall go on forward from there and come to the terebinth tree of Tabor, and three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.
verses.10:4: And they will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you shall receive from their hand.
verses.10:5: After that you shall come to the hill of God, where the garrison of the Philistines is. And it shall come to pass, when you have come there to the city, that you will meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place, with a harp, a tambourine, a flute, and a lyre before them; and they will be prophesying.
verses.10:6: Then the Spirit of the LORD will come mightily upon you, and you will prophesy with them and be turned into another man.
verses.10:7: And let it be, when these signs come to you, that you do for yourself whatever your hand finds to do; for God is with you.
verses.10:8: And you shall go down before me to Gilgal; and behold, I am coming down to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings. Seven days you shall wait until I come to you and make known to you what you shall do."
verses.10:9: And it came to pass, as he turned his shoulder to go from Samuel, that God gave him another heart; and all those signs came to pass on that day.
verses.10:10: When they came there to Gibeah, behold, a band of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God came mightily upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.
verses.10:11: And it came to pass, when all who knew him formerly saw that, behold, he prophesied among the prophets, that the people said one to another, "What is this that has come upon the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.10:12: Then a man from that place answered and said, "And who is their father?" Therefore it became a proverb: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.10:13: And when he had finished prophesying, he came to the high place.
verses.10:14: Then Saul's uncle said to him and to his servant, "Where did you go?" And he said, "To search for the donkeys; and when we saw that they were nowhere to be found, we went to Samuel."
verses.10:15: And Saul's uncle said, "Please tell me what Samuel said to you."
verses.10:16: So Saul said to his uncle, "He plainly told us that the donkeys had been found." But concerning the matter of the kingdom, of which Samuel had spoken, he did not tell him.
verses.10:17: Then Samuel called the people together to the LORD at Mizpah,
verses.10:18: and said to the children of Israel, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I brought up Israel out of Egypt, and delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that were oppressing you.'
verses.10:19: Yet today you have rejected your God, who Himself saves you from all your adversities and your distresses; and you have said to Him, 'Set a king over us!' Now therefore present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your thousands."
verses.10:20: And when Samuel had brought all the tribes of Israel near, the tribe of Benjamin was taken.
verses.10:21: Then he brought the tribe of Benjamin near by its families, and the family of the Matrites was taken. And Saul the son of Kish was taken. But when they sought him, he was not found.
verses.10:22: Therefore they inquired of the LORD further, "Has the man come here yet?" And the LORD answered, "Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage."
verses.10:23: So they ran and brought him from there; and when he stood among the people, he was taller than all the people from his shoulders upward.
verses.10:24: And Samuel said to all the people, "Do you see him whom the LORD has chosen, that there is none like him among all the people?" So all the people shouted and said, "Long live the king!"
verses.10:25: Then Samuel spoke to the people the ordinance of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book and laid it up before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.
verses.10:26: Saul also went to his house at Gibeah; and valiant men went with him, whose hearts God had touched.
verses.10:27: But worthless men said, "How can this man save us?" So they despised him, and brought him no present. But he held his peace.
verses.11:1: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up and encamped against Jabesh Gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, "Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you."
verses.11:2: And Nahash the Ammonite answered them, "On this condition I will make a covenant with you, that I may gouge out every right eye among you, and thus lay a reproach upon all Israel."
verses.11:3: Then the elders of Jabesh said to him, "Grant us seven days' respite, that we may send messengers throughout all the territory of Israel; and then, if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you."
verses.11:4: So the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke these words in the hearing of the people. And all the people lifted up their voices and wept.
verses.11:5: Now behold, Saul was coming behind the oxen from the field; and Saul said, "What troubles the people, that they are weeping?" And they recounted to him the words of the men of Jabesh.
verses.11:6: Then the Spirit of God came mightily upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger was greatly kindled.
verses.11:7: So he took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, "Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen." And the dread of the LORD fell upon the people, and they came out as one man.
verses.11:8: When he mustered them at Bezek, the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
verses.11:9: And they said to the messengers who had come, "Thus shall you say to the men of Jabesh Gilead: 'Tomorrow, by the time the sun grows hot, you shall have deliverance.'" Then the messengers came and told the men of Jabesh, and they were glad.
verses.11:10: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, "Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do with us according to all that seems good in your eyes."
verses.11:11: So it was, on the next day, that Saul divided the people into three companies; and they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch, and struck down the Ammonites until the heat of the day. And it came to pass that those who remained were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
verses.11:12: Then the people said to Samuel, "Who is he who said, 'Shall Saul reign over us?' Bring the men, that we may put them to death."
verses.11:13: But Saul said, "Not a man shall be put to death on this day, for today the LORD has accomplished deliverance in Israel."
verses.11:14: Then Samuel said to the people, "Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingdom there."
verses.11:15: So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. And there they sacrificed peace offerings before the LORD, and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced exceedingly.
verses.12:1: And Samuel said to all Israel, "Behold, I have heeded your voice in all that you have spoken to me, and have set a king over you.
verses.12:2: And now, behold, the king walks before you; as for me, I have grown old and gray-headed, and behold, my sons are with you. And I have walked before you from my youth to this day.
verses.12:3: Here I am. Testify against me before the LORD and before His anointed: Whose ox have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? Or from whose hand have I accepted a bribe to close my eyes with it? And I will restore it to you."
verses.12:4: And they said, "You have not defrauded us, nor have you oppressed us, nor have you taken anything from the hand of any man."
verses.12:5: Then he said to them, "The LORD is witness against you, and His anointed is witness this day, that you have found nothing in my hand." And they replied, "He is witness."
verses.12:6: Then Samuel said to the people, "It is the LORD who appointed Moses and Aaron, and who brought your fathers up from the land of Egypt.
verses.12:7: Now therefore, take your stand, that I may plead with you before the LORD concerning all the righteous deeds of the LORD which He has done with you and with your fathers.
verses.12:8: When Jacob had gone into Egypt, and your fathers cried out to the LORD, then the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.
verses.12:9: Yet they forgot the LORD their God; so He sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.
verses.12:10: Then they cried out to the LORD and said, 'We have sinned, because we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and the Ashtaroth; but now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve You.'
verses.12:11: And the LORD sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and He delivered you from the hand of your enemies on every side, so that you dwelt in safety.
verses.12:12: And when you saw that Nahash king of the sons of Ammon came against you, you said to me, 'No, but a king shall reign over us,' though the LORD your God was your king.
verses.12:13: Now therefore, behold the king whom you have chosen, whom you have asked for! And behold, the LORD has set a king over you.
verses.12:14: If you fear the LORD and serve Him, and heed His voice, and do not rebel against the command of the LORD, then both you and the king who reigns over you shall continue following the LORD your God.
verses.12:15: However, if you do not heed the voice of the LORD, but rebel against the command of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD shall be against you and against your fathers.
verses.12:16: Now therefore, take your stand and behold this great thing which the LORD is about to do before your eyes:
verses.12:17: Is it not wheat harvest today? I will call upon the LORD, and He will send thunder and rain, that you may know and see that your wickedness is great, which you have done in the sight of the LORD, in asking for a king for yourselves."
verses.12:18: So Samuel called upon the LORD, and the LORD sent thunder and rain that day; and all the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel.
verses.12:19: And all the people said to Samuel, "Pray for your servants to the LORD your God, that we may not die; for we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for a king for ourselves."
verses.12:20: Then Samuel said to the people, "Do not fear. You have indeed done all this evil; yet do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.
verses.12:21: And do not turn aside after vain things, which cannot profit or deliver, for they are vanity.
verses.12:22: For the LORD will not forsake His people, for the sake of His great name, because it has pleased the LORD to make you a people for Himself.
verses.12:23: Moreover, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you; but I will instruct you in the good and upright way.
verses.12:24: Only fear the LORD, and serve Him in truth with all your heart; for consider what great things He has done for you.
verses.12:25: Yet if you persist in doing wickedly, both you and your king shall be swept away."
verses.13:2: Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel. Two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. As for the rest of the people, he sent every man away to his tent.
verses.13:3: And Jonathan struck down the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Then Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear!"
verses.13:4: And all Israel heard it said, "Saul has struck down the garrison of the Philistines, and Israel has also become odious to the Philistines." So the people were summoned together after Saul to Gilgal.
verses.13:5: Then the Philistines gathered together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and people like the sand that is on the seashore in multitude. And they came up and encamped in Michmash, to the east of Beth Aven.
verses.13:6: When the men of Israel saw that they were in distress—for the people were hard pressed—the people hid themselves in caves, in thickets, among rocks, in vaults, and in cisterns.
verses.13:7: And some of the Hebrews crossed over the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. As for Saul, he was still in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
verses.13:8: Then he waited seven days, according to the time appointed by Samuel. Yet Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.
verses.13:9: So Saul said, "Bring near to me the burnt offering and the peace offerings." And he offered up the burnt offering.
verses.13:10: And it came to pass, as soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, that behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him, to greet him.
verses.13:11: And Samuel said, "What have you done?" And Saul said, "Because I saw that the people were scattering from me, and that you did not come within the appointed days, and that the Philistines had assembled at Michmash,
verses.13:12: therefore I said, 'Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of the LORD.' So I compelled myself, and offered up the burnt offering."
verses.13:13: And Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God, which He commanded you. For now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
verses.13:14: But now your kingdom shall not stand. The LORD has sought for Himself a man after His own heart, and the LORD has appointed him to be prince over His people, because you have not kept what the LORD commanded you."
verses.13:15: Then Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.
verses.13:16: Now Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people who were present with them, remained in Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines encamped in Michmash.
verses.13:17: And raiders came out from the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned toward the road to Ophrah, to the land of Shual;
verses.13:18: another company turned toward the road to Beth Horon; and another company turned toward the road of the border that overlooks the Valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
verses.13:19: Now no blacksmith was to be found throughout all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, "Lest the Hebrews make swords or spears."
verses.13:20: So all Israel would go down to the Philistines to sharpen each man his plowshare, his mattock, his ax, and his sickle.
verses.13:21: And the charge was a pim for the plowshares, and for the mattocks, and for the three-pronged forks, and for the axes, and to set the goads.
verses.13:22: So it came to pass on the day of battle that neither sword nor spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan; yet they were found with Saul and with Jonathan his son.
verses.13:23: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.
verses.14:1: Now it happened one day that Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armor, "Come, and let us cross over to the garrison of the Philistines that is on the other side." Yet he did not tell his father.
verses.14:2: And Saul was staying at the outskirts of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree that is in Migron, and the people who were with him were about six hundred men.
verses.14:3: And Ahijah the son of Ahitub, the brother of Ichabod, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the priest of the LORD in Shiloh, was bearing an ephod. And the people did not know that Jonathan had departed.
verses.14:4: Now between the passes by which Jonathan sought to cross over to the garrison of the Philistines, there was a crag of rock on one side and a crag of rock on the other side; and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other was Seneh.
verses.14:5: The one crag rose steep on the north opposite Michmash, and the other on the south opposite Geba.
verses.14:6: Then Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armor, "Come, and let us cross over to the garrison of these uncircumcised men; perhaps the LORD will act for us, for there is no restraint upon the LORD to save by many or by few."
verses.14:7: And his armor-bearer said to him, "Do all that is in your heart; turn as you will. Behold, I am with you according to your heart."
verses.14:8: Then Jonathan said, "Behold, we are crossing over to the men, and we will show ourselves to them.
verses.14:9: If they say thus to us, 'Stand still until we come to you,' then we will stand in our place and will not go up to them.
verses.14:10: But if they say thus, 'Come up to us,' then we will go up, for the LORD has delivered them into our hand; and this shall be the sign for us."
verses.14:11: So both of them showed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines. And the Philistines said, "Behold, Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they have hidden themselves!"
verses.14:12: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armor-bearer and said, "Come up to us, and we will make something known to you." Then Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Go up after me, for the LORD has delivered them into the hand of Israel."
verses.14:13: So Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, with his armor-bearer after him; and they fell before Jonathan, while his armor-bearer put them to death behind him.
verses.14:14: And that first slaughter which Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down was about twenty men, within about half a furrow of a yoke of field.
verses.14:15: And there was trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison and the raiding band also trembled, and the earth quaked, so that it became a terror from God.
verses.14:16: Now the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked, and behold, the multitude was melting away and scattering to and fro.
verses.14:17: Then Saul said to the people who were with him, "Take a count now and see who has gone from among us." And when they had taken a count, behold, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.
verses.14:18: And Saul said to Ahijah, "Bring near the ark of God." For the ark of God was on that day with the children of Israel.
verses.14:19: And it came to pass while Saul was speaking to the priest that the tumult in the camp of the Philistines grew more and more; therefore Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hand."
verses.14:20: Then Saul and all the people who were with him rallied together and came to the battle; and behold, every man's sword was against his fellow, in a very great confusion.
verses.14:21: Moreover, the Hebrews who had been with the Philistines before that time, who had gone up with them into the camp from the surrounding country, even they also turned to be with Israel, who were with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.14:22: Likewise all the men of Israel who had hidden themselves in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines had fled, and they also pressed hard after them in the battle.
verses.14:23: So the LORD saved Israel on that day, and the battle passed beyond Beth Aven.
verses.14:24: Now the men of Israel were hard-pressed on that day, for Saul had bound the people with an oath, saying, "Cursed be the man who eats any food until evening, and until I have avenged myself on my enemies." So none of the people tasted any food.
verses.14:25: And all the people of the land entered a forest, and there was honey upon the surface of the field.
verses.14:26: And when the people came into the forest, behold, honey was flowing; yet no one brought his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.
verses.14:27: But Jonathan had not heard when his father bound the people with the oath; therefore he stretched out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and dipped it in a honeycomb, and brought his hand to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.
verses.14:28: Then one of the people spoke up and said, "Your father strictly bound the people with an oath, saying, 'Cursed be the man who eats food this day.'" And the people were faint.
verses.14:29: Then Jonathan said, "My father has troubled the land. Look now, how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
verses.14:30: How much more if the people had eaten freely today of the spoil of their enemies which they found! For now would not the slaughter among the Philistines have been much greater?"
verses.14:31: Now they struck down the Philistines on that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people were exceedingly faint.
verses.14:32: And the people rushed upon the spoil, and took sheep, oxen, and calves, and slaughtered them on the ground; and the people ate them with the blood.
verses.14:33: Then they told Saul, saying, "Behold, the people are sinning against the LORD by eating with the blood." And he said, "You have dealt treacherously; roll a large stone to me today."
verses.14:34: Then Saul said, "Disperse among the people and say to them, 'Bring near to me every man his ox and every man his sheep, and slaughter them here and eat; and do not sin against the LORD by eating with the blood.'" So all the people brought every man his ox by his hand that night and slaughtered them there.
verses.14:35: Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; this was the first altar that he built to the LORD.
verses.14:36: And Saul said, "Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until the light of morning, and let us not leave a man among them." And they said, "Do all that is good in your eyes." Then the priest said, "Let us draw near here to God."
verses.14:37: So Saul inquired of God, "Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will You deliver them into the hand of Israel?" But He did not answer him on that day.
verses.14:38: Then Saul said, "Come near here, all you leaders of the people, and know and see how this sin has happened today.
verses.14:39: For as the LORD lives, who saves Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die." Yet there was not one among all the people who answered him.
verses.14:40: Then he said to all Israel, "You shall be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side." And the people said to Saul, "Do what is good in your eyes."
verses.14:41: Therefore Saul said to the LORD God of Israel, "Give a true lot." And Jonathan and Saul were taken, while the people went free.
verses.14:42: And Saul said, "Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son." And Jonathan was taken.
verses.14:43: Then Saul said to Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." And Jonathan told him and said, "I indeed tasted a little honey with the tip of the staff that was in my hand; behold, I must die."
verses.14:44: And Saul said, "May God do so and more also; for you shall surely die, Jonathan."
verses.14:45: But the people said to Saul, "Shall Jonathan die, who has accomplished this great salvation in Israel? Far be it! As the LORD lives, not a single hair of his head shall fall to the ground, for he has worked with God this day." So the people ransomed Jonathan, and he did not die.
verses.14:46: Then Saul went up from pursuing the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place.
verses.14:47: So Saul secured the kingship over Israel, and fought against all his enemies on every side: against Moab, against the children of Ammon, against Edom, against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines; and wherever he turned, he inflicted defeat.
verses.14:48: And he acted valiantly, and struck down Amalek, and delivered Israel from the hand of those who plundered them.
verses.14:49: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua; and the names of his two daughters were these: the name of the firstborn was Merab, and the name of the younger was Michal.
verses.14:50: And the name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam the daughter of Ahimaaz; and the name of the commander of his army was Abner the son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
verses.14:51: And Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
verses.14:52: Now there was fierce war against the Philistines all the days of Saul; and whenever Saul saw any mighty man or any valiant man, he gathered him to himself.
verses.15:1: And Samuel said to Saul, "The LORD sent me to anoint you as king over His people, over Israel. Now therefore, listen to the voice of the words of the LORD.
verses.15:2: Thus says the LORD of hosts: 'I have taken account of what Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him on the way when he came up out of Egypt.
verses.15:3: Now go and strike Amalek, and utterly devote to destruction all that belongs to him, and do not spare him; rather, put to death from man to woman, from child to nursing infant, from ox to sheep, from camel to donkey.'"
verses.15:4: So Saul summoned the people and mustered them at Telaim, two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah.
verses.15:5: And Saul came to the city of Amalek, and set an ambush in the valley.
verses.15:6: Then Saul said to the Kenites, "Go, depart, go down from the midst of the Amalekites, lest I sweep you away with them; for you showed lovingkindness to all the children of Israel when they came up out of Egypt." So the Kenites departed from the midst of Amalek.
verses.15:7: And Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as far as Shur, which lies east of Egypt.
verses.15:8: He also seized Agag king of Amalek alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.
verses.15:9: But Saul and the people spared Agag and the choicest of the sheep and the oxen, the fatlings and the lambs, and all that was good, and they were unwilling to utterly destroy them; yet everything despised and worthless, that they utterly destroyed.
verses.15:10: Now the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,
verses.15:11: "I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned back from following Me, and has not fulfilled My words." And Samuel was deeply distressed, and he cried out to the LORD all night.
verses.15:12: So Samuel rose early in the morning to meet Saul; and it was reported to Samuel, saying, "Saul came to Carmel, and behold, he set up a monument for himself, and turned about, passed on, and went down to Gilgal."
verses.15:13: Then Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, "Blessed are you of the LORD! I have fulfilled the word of the LORD."
verses.15:14: But Samuel said, "What then is this sound of sheep in my ears, and the sound of oxen that I am hearing?"
verses.15:15: And Saul said, "From the Amalekites they have brought them, for the people spared the choicest of the sheep and the oxen to sacrifice to the LORD your God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed."
verses.15:16: Then Samuel said to Saul, "Stop, and let me declare to you what the LORD spoke to me this past night." And he said to him, "Speak."
verses.15:17: So Samuel said, "Though you are little in your own eyes, are you not the head of the tribes of Israel? And the LORD anointed you as king over Israel.
verses.15:18: Furthermore, the LORD sent you on a mission and said, 'Go and utterly destroy the sinners, the Amalekites, and fight against them until they are consumed.'
verses.15:19: Why then did you not obey the voice of the LORD, but swooped down upon the spoil and did evil in the sight of the LORD?"
verses.15:20: And Saul said to Samuel, "Indeed I have obeyed the voice of the LORD, and have gone on the way upon which the LORD sent me; I have brought back Agag king of Amalek, and I have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.
verses.15:21: Yet the people took from the spoil sheep and oxen, the choicest of the things devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God in Gilgal."
verses.15:22: Then Samuel said, "Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to give heed than the fat of rams.
verses.15:23: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and presumption is like iniquity and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He also has rejected you from being king."
verses.15:24: Then Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned, for I have transgressed the command of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and listened to their voice.
verses.15:25: And now, please pardon my sin, and turn back with me, that I may worship the LORD."
verses.15:26: But Samuel said to Saul, "I will not return with you, for you have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel."
verses.15:27: And as Samuel turned to depart, Saul seized the hem of his robe, and it tore.
verses.15:28: Then Samuel said to him, "The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you this day, and has given it to a neighbor of yours who is better than you.
verses.15:29: And moreover, the Glory of Israel will not lie nor relent; for He is not a man, that He should relent."
verses.15:30: Then he said, "I have sinned; yet honor me now, please, before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me, that I may worship the LORD your God."
verses.15:31: So Samuel turned back after Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.
verses.15:32: Then Samuel said, "Bring near to me Agag king of Amalek." So Agag came to him cheerfully, and Agag said, "Surely the bitterness of death has departed."
verses.15:33: But Samuel said, "As your sword has bereaved women of children, so shall your mother be bereaved among women." And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the LORD in Gilgal.
verses.15:34: Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.
verses.15:35: And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death; yet Samuel mourned over Saul, and the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.
verses.16:1: Now the LORD said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn over Saul, seeing that I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go; I am sending you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided for Myself a king among his sons."
verses.16:2: And Samuel said, "How can I go? If Saul hears of it, he will slay me." Then the LORD said, "Take a heifer from the herd with you, and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.'
verses.16:3: Then invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do; and you shall anoint for Me the one whom I name to you."
verses.16:4: So Samuel did what the LORD had spoken, and came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the city came trembling to meet him, and said, "Is your coming in peace?"
verses.16:5: And he said, "In peace; I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice." Then he consecrated Jesse and his sons, and invited them to the sacrifice.
verses.16:6: Now it came to pass, when they arrived, that he looked on Eliab and said, "Surely before the LORD stands His anointed!"
verses.16:7: But the LORD said to Samuel, "Do not gaze upon his appearance or upon the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. For it is not as man sees: man looks to the outward appearance, whereas the LORD looks to the heart."
verses.16:8: Then Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, "Neither has the LORD chosen this one."
verses.16:9: Then Jesse made Shammah pass by. And he said, "Neither has the LORD chosen this one."
verses.16:10: Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse, "The LORD has not chosen these."
verses.16:11: And Samuel said to Jesse, "Are all the young men here?" Then he said, "There still remains the youngest, and behold, he is tending the flock." And Samuel said to Jesse, "Send and bring him, for we will not sit down until he comes here."
verses.16:12: So he sent and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with handsome eyes and a pleasing appearance. And the LORD said, "Arise, anoint him, for this is the one!"
verses.16:13: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brethren; and the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon David from that day forward. So Samuel arose and went to Ramah.
verses.16:14: Now the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD tormented him.
verses.16:15: And Saul's servants said to him, "Behold now, an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.
verses.16:16: Let our lord now command your servants who stand before you to seek out a man who is skilled in playing the harp; and it shall be, when an evil spirit from God is upon you, that he shall play with his hand, and you shall be well."
verses.16:17: So Saul said to his servants, "Provide for me now a man who plays well, and bring him to me."
verses.16:18: Then one of the young men answered and said, "Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, who is skilled in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, discerning in speech, and a man of handsome form; and the LORD is with him."
verses.16:19: Therefore Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, "Send to me David your son, who is with the flock."
verses.16:20: And Jesse took a donkey laden with bread, a skin of wine, and one young goat, and sent them by the hand of David his son to Saul.
verses.16:21: So David came to Saul and stood before him; and Saul loved him greatly, and he became his armorbearer.
verses.16:22: Then Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, "Please let David stand before me, for he has found favor in my sight."
verses.16:23: And so it was, whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, that David would take the harp and play with his hand; then relief would come to Saul and he would be well, and the evil spirit would depart from him.
verses.17:1: Now the Philistines gathered their hosts together for battle, and they assembled at Socoh, which belongs to Judah; and they encamped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.
verses.17:2: And Saul and the men of Israel assembled together, and encamped in the Valley of Elah, and drew up the battle line to meet the Philistines.
verses.17:3: And the Philistines stood on the mountain on one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side, and the valley was between them.
verses.17:4: And a champion came forth from the camps of the Philistines, whose name was Goliath, from Gath; his height was six cubits and a span.
verses.17:5: He had a helmet of bronze upon his head, and he was clad in a coat of scale armor; and the weight of the armor was five thousand shekels of bronze.
verses.17:6: And bronze greaves were upon his legs, and a bronze javelin was between his shoulders.
verses.17:7: And the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and the blade of his spear weighed six hundred shekels of iron; and the shield-bearer went before him.
verses.17:8: And he stood and cried out to the ranks of Israel, and said to them, "Why do you come forth to draw up for battle? Am I not the Philistine, and you the servants of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
verses.17:9: If he is able to fight with me and slay me, then we will become your servants; but if I prevail against him and slay him, then you shall become our servants and serve us."
verses.17:10: And the Philistine said, "I defy the ranks of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together."
verses.17:11: When Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and exceedingly afraid.
verses.17:32: Then David said to Saul, "Let no man's heart fail on account of him; your servant will go and do battle with this Philistine."
verses.17:33: And Saul said to David, "You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him; for you are a youth, and he has been a man of war from his youth."
verses.17:34: But David said to Saul, "Your servant was keeping his father's flock, and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the herd,
verses.17:35: I went out after it and struck it, and rescued it from its mouth; and when it rose up against me, I seized it by its beard, and struck it and slew it.
verses.17:36: Your servant has struck down both the lion and the bear; and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them, because he has defied the ranks of the living God."
verses.17:37: Moreover David said, "The LORD, who delivered me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, He will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine." And Saul said to David, "Go, and the LORD be with you."
verses.17:38: Then Saul clothed David with his own battle garments, and put a helmet of bronze upon his head; he also clothed him with a coat of mail.
verses.17:39: And David girded his sword over his battle garments, and tried to walk, for he had not tested them. And David said to Saul, "I am not able to walk in these, for I have not tested them." So David put them off from himself.
verses.17:40: Then he took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five smooth stones from the brook, and placed them in the shepherd's bag that he had, even in the pouch; and his sling was in his hand. And he drew near to the Philistine.
verses.17:42: And when the Philistine looked and saw David, he disdained him; for he was a youth, ruddy and of fair appearance.
verses.17:43: So the Philistine said to David, "Am I a dog, that you come to me with staves?" And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
verses.17:44: And the Philistine said to David, "Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and to the beasts of the field."
verses.17:45: Then David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the ranks of Israel, whom you have defied.
verses.17:46: This day the LORD will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you down and sever your head from you; and this day I will give the carcasses of the host of the Philistines to the birds of the heavens and to the wild beasts of the earth, that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.
verses.17:47: And all this assembly shall know that the LORD does not deliver with sword and spear; for the battle belongs to the LORD, and He will give you into our hand."
verses.17:48: And it came to pass, when the Philistine arose and came forward and drew near to meet David, that David hastened and ran toward the battle line to meet the Philistine.
verses.17:49: Then David reached his hand into the bag and took from there a stone, and slung it and struck the Philistine on his forehead; and the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the earth.
verses.17:51: Therefore David ran and stood over the Philistine, and took his sword and drew it out of its sheath, and put him to death, and cut off his head with it. And when the Philistines saw that their mighty champion was dead, they fled.
verses.17:52: Then the men of Israel and Judah arose and shouted, and pursued the Philistines as far as the entrance to the valley and to the gates of Ekron. And the slain of the Philistines fell along the way to Shaaraim, even as far as Gath and Ekron.
verses.17:53: And the children of Israel returned from hotly pursuing the Philistines, and they plundered their camps.
verses.17:54: And David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, but his armor he placed in his tent.
verses.18:6: Now it came to pass as they were coming home, when David returned from striking down the Philistine, that the women came out from all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet King Saul, with timbrels, with joy, and with three-stringed instruments.
verses.18:7: And the women sang to one another as they made merry, and said, "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands."
verses.18:8: Then Saul was exceedingly angry, and this saying was displeasing in his eyes; and he said, "They have ascribed to David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed the thousands; and what more remains for him except the kingdom?"
verses.18:9: So Saul eyed David with suspicion from that day onward.
verses.18:12: Now Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with him, but had departed from Saul.
verses.18:13: Therefore Saul removed him from his presence, and appointed him as his commander over a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people.
verses.18:14: And David acted wisely in all his ways, and the LORD was with him.
verses.18:15: Therefore, when Saul saw that he acted very wisely, he stood in dread of him.
verses.18:16: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them.
verses.18:20: Now Michal, the daughter of Saul, loved David. And they told Saul, and the matter was pleasing in his eyes.
verses.18:21: And Saul said, "I will give her to him, that she may become a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be upon him." Therefore Saul said to David, "A second time you shall become my son-in-law this day."
verses.18:22: And Saul commanded his servants, "Speak to David in secret, saying, 'Behold, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you; now therefore, become the king's son-in-law.'"
verses.18:23: So the servants of Saul spoke these words in the ears of David. And David said, "Is it a light thing in your eyes to become the king's son-in-law, seeing that I am a poor man and lightly esteemed?"
verses.18:24: And the servants of Saul told him, saying, "According to these words David has spoken."
verses.18:25: Then Saul said, "Thus you shall say to David, 'The king has no desire for a bride-price, except for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to take vengeance upon the king's enemies.'" Now Saul purposed to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.
verses.18:26: When his servants told David these words, the matter was pleasing in the eyes of David to become the king's son-in-law. And the appointed days had not yet been fulfilled.
verses.18:27: Therefore David arose and went, he and his men, and struck down two hundred men among the Philistines; and David brought their foreskins, and they delivered them in full count to the king, that he might become the king's son-in-law. Then Saul gave him Michal his daughter as a wife.
verses.18:28: And Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David, and that Michal, the daughter of Saul, loved him.
verses.18:29: Thus Saul feared David yet the more; and Saul became David's enemy continually.
verses.19:1: Now Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants, that they should put David to death; but Jonathan the son of Saul delighted greatly in David.
verses.19:2: So Jonathan told David, saying, "Saul my father is seeking to put you to death. Now therefore, please watch carefully in the morning, and abide in a secret place and hide yourself.
verses.19:3: And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak with my father concerning you. Then what I see, I will declare to you."
verses.19:4: Then Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father, and said to him, "Do not let the king sin against his servant, against David, for he has not sinned against you, and his deeds have been exceedingly good toward you.
verses.19:5: For he put his life in his hand and struck down the Philistine, and the LORD worked a great deliverance for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced. Why then will you sin against innocent blood, by putting David to death without cause?"
verses.19:6: So Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore, "As the LORD lives, he shall not be put to death."
