verses.19:7: Then Jonathan called David, and Jonathan told him all these words. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as in times past.
verses.19:8: And there was war again; and David went out and fought with the Philistines, and struck them with a great slaughter, so that they fled before him.
verses.19:9: Now an evil spirit from the LORD came upon Saul while he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand, and David was playing music with his hand.
verses.19:10: And Saul sought to pin David to the wall with the spear, but he slipped away from before Saul, so that he drove the spear into the wall. And David fled and escaped that night.
verses.19:11: Saul also sent messengers to the house of David to watch him and to put him to death in the morning. And Michal his wife told David, saying, "If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be put to death."
verses.19:12: So Michal let David down through the window; and he went and fled and escaped.
verses.19:13: And Michal took the household idol and laid it on the bed, put a quilt of goats' hair at its head, and covered it with a garment.
verses.19:14: And when Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, "He is sick."
verses.19:15: Then Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, "Bring him up to me on the bed, that I may put him to death."
verses.19:16: And when the messengers came in, behold, the household idol was on the bed, with the quilt of goats' hair at its head.
verses.19:17: Then Saul said to Michal, "Why have you deceived me like this, and sent away my enemy so that he has escaped?" And Michal answered Saul, "He said to me, 'Let me go! Why should I put you to death?'"
verses.19:18: So David fled and escaped, and came to Samuel at Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and dwelt in Naioth.
verses.19:19: And it was told to Saul, saying, "Behold, David is in Naioth in Ramah."
verses.19:20: Then Saul sent messengers to take David. And when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing as leader over them, the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied.
verses.19:21: When they told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saul sent messengers again a third time, and they also prophesied.
verses.19:22: Then he himself also went to Ramah, and came as far as the great cistern that is in Secu. And he asked and said, "Where are Samuel and David?" And one said, "Behold, they are in Naioth in Ramah."
verses.19:23: So he went there to Naioth in Ramah. And the Spirit of God came upon him also, and he went on prophesying continuously until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
verses.19:24: He also stripped off his garments, and he too prophesied before Samuel, and fell down naked all that day and all that night. Therefore they say, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.20:1: Then David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and came and said before Jonathan, "What have I done? What is my iniquity, and what is my sin before your father, that he seeks my life?"
verses.20:2: And he said to him, "Far be it! You shall not die. Behold, my father does nothing, either great or small, without revealing it to me. And why should my father conceal this thing from me? It is not so!"
verses.20:3: Then David swore again and said, "Your father certainly knows that I have found favor in your sight, and he has said, 'Do not let Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved.' Yet truly, as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, there is but a step between me and death."
verses.20:4: Then Jonathan said to David, "Whatever your soul desires, I will do for you."
verses.20:5: And David said to Jonathan, "Behold, tomorrow is the New Moon, and I ought indeed to sit with the king to eat; but let me go, that I may hide myself in the field until the third evening.
verses.20:6: If your father misses me at all, then you shall say, 'David earnestly asked leave of me that he might hasten to Bethlehem his city, for there is a yearly sacrifice there for all the family.'
verses.20:7: If he says thus, 'It is well,' your servant will have peace; but if he is greatly angered, know that evil is determined by him.
verses.20:8: Therefore show lovingkindness to your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the LORD with you. Yet if there is iniquity in me, put me to death yourself; why then should you bring me to your father?"
verses.20:9: And Jonathan said, "Far be it from you! For if I knew certainly that evil was determined by my father to come upon you, would I not tell you about it?"
verses.20:10: Then David said to Jonathan, "Who will tell me, or what if your father answers you harshly?"
verses.20:11: And Jonathan said to David, "Come, and let us go out into the field." So the two of them went out into the field.
verses.20:12: Then Jonathan said to David, "By the LORD, the God of Israel, when I have sounded out my father about this time tomorrow, or the third day, and behold, there is goodwill toward David, shall I not then send to you and reveal it to you?
verses.20:13: May the LORD do so to Jonathan, and much more also! If it pleases my father to do you evil, then I will reveal it to you and send you away, that you may go in peace. And may the LORD be with you as He has been with my father.
verses.20:14: And not only while I am still alive shall you show me the lovingkindness of the LORD, that I may not die;
verses.20:15: but you shall not cut off your lovingkindness from my house forever—no, not even when the LORD has cut off every one of the enemies of David from the face of the earth."
verses.20:16: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David: "May the LORD require it at the hand of David's enemies."
verses.20:17: And Jonathan made David swear again because of his love for him, for he loved him as his own soul.
verses.20:18: Then Jonathan said to him, "Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be empty.
verses.20:19: And when you have stayed three days, go down quickly and come to the place where you hid yourself on the day of the affair, and abide beside the stone Ezel.
verses.20:20: And I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as though I were shooting at a target.
verses.20:21: And behold, I will send the lad, saying, 'Go, find the arrows.' If I expressly say to the lad, 'Behold, the arrows are on this side of you, take them,' then come; for there is peace for you and no harm, as the LORD lives.
verses.20:22: But if I say thus to the young man, 'Behold, the arrows are beyond you,' go your way, for the LORD has sent you away.
verses.20:23: And as for the matter of which we have spoken, I and you, behold, the LORD is between me and you forever."
verses.20:24: So David hid himself in the field. And when the New Moon came, the king sat down to the meal to eat.
verses.20:25: Now the king sat upon his seat, as at other times, upon the seat by the wall. And Jonathan arose, and Abner sat by Saul's side, but David's place was empty.
verses.20:26: Yet Saul did not speak anything that day, for he thought, "Something has befallen him; he is not clean—surely he is not clean."
verses.20:27: And it came to pass on the day after the New Moon, the second day, that David's place was empty. And Saul said to Jonathan his son, "Why has the son of Jesse not come to the meal, either yesterday or today?"
verses.20:28: So Jonathan answered Saul, "David earnestly asked leave of me to go to Bethlehem.
verses.20:29: And he said, 'Please let me go, for our family has a sacrifice in the city, and my brother himself has commanded me to be there. And now, if I have found favor in your sight, please let me slip away and see my brethren.' Therefore he has not come to the king's table."
verses.20:30: Then Saul's anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, "You son of a perverse, rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own shame, and to the shame of your mother's nakedness?
verses.20:31: For as long as the son of Jesse lives upon the earth, neither you nor your kingdom shall be established. Now therefore, send and bring him to me, for he shall surely die!"
verses.20:32: And Jonathan answered Saul his father, and said to him, "Why should he be put to death? What has he done?"
verses.20:33: Then Saul hurled the spear at him to strike him; so Jonathan knew that it was determined by his father to put David to death.
verses.20:34: So Jonathan arose from the table in fierce anger, and ate no food on the second day of the month, for he was grieved for David, because his father had dishonored him.
verses.20:35: And it came to pass in the morning that Jonathan went out into the field at the time appointed with David, and a little lad was with him.
verses.20:36: Then he said to his lad, "Run, please find the arrows which I shoot." As the lad ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
verses.20:37: And when the lad came to the place of the arrow which Jonathan had shot, Jonathan cried out after the lad and said, "Is not the arrow beyond you?"
verses.20:38: And Jonathan cried out after the lad, "Hurry, make haste, do not stand still!" So Jonathan's lad gathered up the arrows and came to his master.
verses.20:39: Now the lad knew nothing; only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
verses.20:40: Then Jonathan gave his weapons to his lad, and said to him, "Go, carry them to the city."
verses.20:41: As soon as the lad had gone, David arose from the south side, and fell on his face to the ground and bowed down three times. And they kissed one another and wept together, David even more.
verses.20:42: Then Jonathan said to David, "Go in peace, since we have both sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, 'The LORD shall be between me and you, and between my descendants and your descendants, forever.'"
verses.21:1: Then he arose and departed, and Jonathan went into the city.
verses.21:2: And David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest; and Ahimelech trembled at meeting David, and said to him, "Why are you alone, and no man is with you?"
verses.21:3: And David said to Ahimelech the priest, "The king has commanded me on a matter, and said to me, 'Let no man know anything of the matter about which I am sending you and which I have commanded you.' And I have appointed the young men to such and such a place.
verses.21:4: Now therefore, what is under your hand? Give five loaves of bread into my hand, or whatever is found."
verses.21:5: Then the priest answered David and said, "There is no common bread under my hand, but there is holy bread—if only the young men have kept themselves from women."
verses.21:6: And David answered the priest and said to him, "Truly, women have been kept from us for about three days since I came out, and the vessels of the young men are holy, even though the journey is common; how much more today shall it be holy in the vessel!"
verses.21:7: So the priest gave him holy bread; for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD, in order to set out warm bread on the day it was taken away.
verses.21:8: Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the LORD; and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of the herdsmen who belonged to Saul.
verses.21:9: And David said to Ahimelech, "Is there not here under your hand a spear or a sword? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons in my hand, because the king's business was urgent."
verses.21:10: And the priest said, "The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the Valley of Elah—behold, it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you wish to take that for yourself, take it, for there is no other besides it here." And David said, "There is none like it; give it to me."
verses.21:11: Then David arose and fled that day from before Saul, and came to Achish the king of Gath.
verses.21:12: And the servants of Achish said to him, "Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing in response concerning this man in the dances, saying, 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
verses.21:13: And David laid these words to his heart, and feared exceedingly before Achish the king of Gath.
verses.21:14: So he disguised his sanity before their eyes, and feigned madness in their hands; and he scratched marks on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle run down upon his beard.
verses.21:15: Then Achish said to his servants, "Behold, you see the man is mad. Why have you brought him to me?
verses.21:16: Am I lacking in madmen, that you have brought this man to behave like a madman in my presence? Shall this man come into my house?"
verses.22:1: So David departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. And when his brethren and all his father's house heard of it, they went down to him there.
verses.22:2: And every man who was in distress, and every man who was in debt, and every man who was bitter of soul gathered to him; and he became commander over them. And there were with him about four hundred men.
verses.22:3: Then David went from there to Mizpeh of Moab, and said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and my mother come and stay with you, until I know what God will do for me."
verses.22:4: So he brought them before the king of Moab, and they dwelt with him all the days that David was in the stronghold.
verses.22:5: Now the prophet Gad said to David, "Do not remain in the stronghold; depart, and go into the land of Judah." So David departed and came into the forest of Hereth.
verses.22:6: And Saul heard that David and the men who were with him had been discovered. Now Saul was sitting in Gibeah under the tamarisk tree on the height, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him.
verses.22:7: Then Saul said to his servants who were standing around him, "Hear now, you Benjaminites! Will the son of Jesse also give to every one of you fields and vineyards, and make every one of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds,
verses.22:8: that all of you have conspired against me, and there is none who informs me when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse; and there is none among you who grieves for me or informs me that my son has stirred up my servant against me to lie in wait, as at this day?"
verses.22:9: Then Doeg the Edomite, who was set over the servants of Saul, answered and said, "I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
verses.22:10: And he inquired of the LORD for him, and gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine."
verses.22:11: Then the king sent to summon Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, the priest, and all his father's house, the priests who were in Nob; and all of them came to the king.
verses.22:12: And Saul said, "Hear now, son of Ahitub." And he answered, "Here I am, my lord."
verses.22:13: Then Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you have given him bread and a sword, and have inquired of God for him, that he should rise against me to lie in wait, as at this day?"
verses.22:14: So Ahimelech answered the king and said, "And who among all your servants is as faithful as David, who is the king's son-in-law, and goes at your bidding, and is honored in your house?
verses.22:15: Did I begin today to inquire of God for him? Far be it from me! Do not let the king impute anything to his servant, nor to all the house of my father; for your servant knew nothing of all this, whether small or great."
verses.22:16: And the king said, "You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father's house."
verses.22:17: Then the king said to the guards who stood around him, "Turn and put to death the priests of the LORD, because their hand also is with David, and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not inform me." But the servants of the king were not willing to stretch out their hand to strike the priests of the LORD.
verses.22:18: And the king said to Doeg, "You turn and strike the priests." So Doeg the Edomite turned and struck the priests himself, and put to death on that day eighty-five men who wore a linen ephod.
verses.22:19: And Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the edge of the sword—both men and women, children and nursing infants, oxen and donkeys and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
verses.22:20: Now one son of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, whose name was Abiathar, escaped and fled after David.
verses.22:21: And Abiathar told David that Saul had slain the priests of the LORD.
verses.22:22: So David said to Abiathar, "I knew on that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I have occasioned the death of every person of your father's house.
verses.22:23: Abide with me; do not fear. For he who seeks my life seeks your life; indeed, with me you shall be in safekeeping."
verses.23:1: Then they told David, saying, "Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and they are plundering the threshing floors."
verses.23:2: Therefore David inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I go and strike these Philistines?" And the LORD said to David, "Go and strike the Philistines, and deliver Keilah."
verses.23:3: But David's men said to him, "Behold, we are afraid here in Judah. How much more then if we go to Keilah against the battle lines of the Philistines?"
verses.23:4: So David inquired of the LORD once again. And the LORD answered him and said, "Arise, go down to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand."
verses.23:5: And David and his men went to Keilah and fought against the Philistines, drove away their livestock, and struck them with a great slaughter. So David delivered the inhabitants of Keilah.
verses.23:6: Now it came to pass, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, that he came down with an ephod in his hand.
verses.23:7: And it was told to Saul that David had come to Keilah. And Saul said, "God has delivered him into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a city that has gates and bars."
verses.23:8: Then Saul summoned all the people for war, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men.
verses.23:9: When David knew that Saul was plotting evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod near."
verses.23:10: Then David said, "O LORD God of Israel, Your servant has certainly heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah to destroy the city on my account.
verses.23:11: Will the lords of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as Your servant has heard? O LORD God of Israel, I pray, tell Your servant." And the LORD said, "He will come down."
verses.23:13: Then David and his men, about six hundred men, arose and departed from Keilah, and went wherever they could go. And it was told to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, so he refrained from going out.
verses.23:14: And David abode in strongholds in the wilderness, and remained in the hill country in the Wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God did not deliver him into his hand.
verses.23:15: And David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life; and David was in the Wilderness of Ziph at Horesh.
verses.23:16: Then Jonathan, Saul's son, arose and went to David at Horesh, and strengthened his hand in God.
verses.23:17: And he said to him, "Do not fear, for the hand of Saul my father shall not find you. You shall reign over Israel, and I shall be second to you. Even Saul my father knows this."
verses.23:18: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. And David remained at Horesh, and Jonathan went to his house.
verses.23:19: Then the Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Is David not hiding with us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, which is south of Jeshimon?
verses.23:20: Now therefore, O king, come down according to all the desire of your soul to come down; and our part shall be to surrender him into the king's hand."
verses.23:21: And Saul said, "Blessed are you of the LORD, for you have had compassion on me.
verses.23:22: Please go, make yet more certain, and learn and see his place where his foot is, and who has seen him there; for it has been told to me that he deals very craftily.
verses.23:23: See therefore, and take knowledge of all the hiding places where he conceals himself, and return to me with certainty, and I will go with you. And it shall be, if he is in the land, that I will search him out throughout all the thousands of Judah."
verses.23:24: So they arose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the Wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah to the south of Jeshimon.
verses.23:25: When Saul and his men went to seek him, they told David; therefore he went down to the rock and stayed in the Wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard that, he pursued after David in the Wilderness of Maon.
verses.23:26: Then Saul went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men on the other side of the mountain. And David made haste to get away from before Saul, for Saul and his men were encircling David and his men to seize them.
verses.23:27: But a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Hasten and come, for the Philistines have raided the land!"
verses.23:28: Therefore Saul returned from pursuing after David, and went to meet the Philistines; for that reason they called that place the Rock of Divisions.
verses.24:1: Then David went up from there and dwelt in the strongholds of En Gedi.
verses.24:2: Now it came to pass, when Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, that they told him, saying, "Behold, David is in the wilderness of En Gedi."
verses.24:3: So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
verses.24:4: And he came to the sheepfolds along the way, where there was a cave; and Saul entered to cover his feet, while David and his men were sitting in the recesses of the cave.
verses.24:5: Then the men of David said to him, "Behold, this is the day of which the LORD said to you, 'Behold, I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it seems good in your eyes.'" So David arose and stealthily cut off a corner of Saul's robe.
verses.24:6: And it came to pass afterward that David's heart struck him because he had cut off the corner of Saul's robe.
verses.24:7: And he said to his men, "The LORD forbid that I should do this thing to my lord, the LORD's anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, for he is the anointed of the LORD."
verses.24:8: So David restrained his men with these words, and did not permit them to rise against Saul. And Saul rose up from the cave and went on his way.
verses.24:9: David also arose afterward, went out of the cave, and called after Saul, saying, "My lord the king!" And when Saul looked behind him, David bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself.
verses.24:10: And David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to the words of men who say, 'Behold, David seeks your harm'?
verses.24:11: Behold, this day your eyes have seen how the LORD delivered you today into my hand in the cave, and some urged me to kill you; yet I spared you, and I said, 'I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is the anointed of the LORD.'
verses.24:12: Moreover, my father, see—yes, see the corner of your robe in my hand! For in that I cut off the corner of your robe and did not kill you, know and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against you, yet you hunt my life to take it.
verses.24:13: May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me on you; yet my hand shall not be against you.
verses.24:14: As the proverb of the ancients says, 'Wickedness proceeds from the wicked.' Yet my hand shall not be against you.
verses.24:15: After whom has the king of Israel come out? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog? After a single flea?
verses.24:16: May the LORD therefore be judge, and execute judgment between me and you, and look and plead my cause, and vindicate me out of your hand."
verses.24:17: Now it came to pass, when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
verses.24:18: Then he said to David, "You are more righteous than I; for you have repaid me with good, whereas I have repaid you with evil.
verses.24:19: And you have shown this day how you have dealt well with me, in that when the LORD delivered me into your hand, you did not kill me.
verses.24:20: For if a man finds his enemy, will he send him away safely on his way? Therefore may the LORD reward you with good for what you have done to me this day.
verses.24:21: And now, behold, I know indeed that you shall surely reign, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in your hand.
verses.24:22: Therefore swear now to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my descendants after me, and that you will not destroy my name from my father's house."
verses.24:23: So David swore to Saul. And Saul went to his own house, while David and his men went up to the stronghold.
verses.25:1: Now Samuel died, and all Israel gathered together and lamented for him, and buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David arose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
verses.25:2: And there was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel, and the man was very wealthy. He had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
verses.25:3: Now the name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife was Abigail. And the woman was of good understanding and fair in appearance; yet the man was harsh and evil in his doings, and he was a Calebite.
verses.25:4: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
verses.25:5: So David sent ten young men; and David said to the young men, "Go up to Carmel, go to Nabal, and greet him in my name.
verses.25:6: And thus you shall say: 'Long life to you! Peace be to you, peace to your house, and peace to all that belongs to you.
verses.25:7: Now I have heard that you have shearers. Your shepherds were with us, and we did not mistreat them, nor was anything missing to them all the days they were in Carmel.
verses.25:8: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Therefore let the young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a festive day. Please give whatever comes to your hand to your servants and to your son David.'"
verses.25:9: So when David's young men came, they spoke to Nabal according to all these words in the name of David, and waited.
verses.25:10: Then Nabal answered David's servants and said, "Who is David, and who is the son of Jesse? There are many servants nowadays who break away, each one from his master.
verses.25:11: Shall I then take my bread and my water and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men when I do not know where they are from?"
verses.25:12: So David's young men turned back on their way, and returned and came and reported to him according to all these words.
verses.25:13: Then David said to his men, "Every man gird on his sword." So every man girded on his sword, and David also girded on his sword. And about four hundred men went up after David, while two hundred remained with the baggage.
verses.25:14: Now one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, saying, "Behold, David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, and he railed at them.
verses.25:15: Yet the men were very good to us; we were not mistreated, nor did we miss anything all the days we went about with them while we were in the field.
verses.25:16: They were a wall around us both by night and by day, all the days we were with them tending the sheep.
verses.25:17: Now therefore, know and consider what you will do, for harm is determined against our master and against all his household; and he is such a worthless man that one cannot speak to him."
verses.25:18: Then Abigail made haste and took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five sheep already dressed, five seahs of roasted grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and loaded them on donkeys.
verses.25:19: And she said to her young men, "Go on before me; behold, I am coming after you." Yet she did not tell her husband Nabal.
verses.25:20: And it happened, as she rode on the donkey and went down under cover of the mountain, that behold, David and his men were coming down toward her; and she met them.
verses.25:21: Now David had said, "Surely in vain have I guarded all that this fellow has in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that belongs to him; and he has repaid me evil for good.
verses.25:22: May God do so, and more also, to the enemies of David, if I leave of all who belong to him even a single male by morning."
verses.25:23: Now when Abigail saw David, she hastened and dismounted from the donkey, and fell on her face before David and bowed to the ground.
verses.25:24: So she fell at his feet and said, "On me, my lord, on me alone be this iniquity! And please let your maidservant speak in your ears, and hear the words of your maidservant.
verses.25:25: Please, do not let my lord pay attention to this worthless man, Nabal; for as his name is, so is he—Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. Yet I, your maidservant, did not see the young men of my lord whom you sent.
verses.25:26: Now therefore, my lord, as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, since the LORD has restrained you from coming to bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hand, now let your enemies and those who seek harm against my lord be like Nabal.
verses.25:27: And now this present which your handmaid has brought to my lord, let it be given to the young men who follow my lord.
verses.25:28: Please forgive the transgression of your maidservant. For the LORD will surely make for my lord an enduring house, because my lord fights the battles of the LORD, and evil shall not be found in you throughout all your days.
verses.25:29: And though a man should rise up to pursue you and seek your life, yet the life of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God; and the lives of your enemies He shall sling out as from the hollow of a sling.
verses.25:30: And it shall come to pass, when the LORD has done for my lord according to all the good that He has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you ruler over Israel,
verses.25:31: that this shall be no grief to you, nor a stumbling block of heart to my lord, either that you have shed blood without cause, or that my lord has avenged himself. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, then remember your maidservant."
verses.25:32: Then David said to Abigail, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me!
verses.25:33: And blessed be your discernment, and blessed be you, who have kept me this day from coming to bloodshed and from avenging myself with my own hand.
verses.25:34: For indeed, as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has restrained me from doing harm to you, unless you had hurried and come to meet me, surely by morning light there would not have been left to Nabal even a single male."
verses.25:35: So David received from her hand what she had brought him, and said to her, "Go up in peace to your house. See, I have heeded your voice and honored your request."
verses.25:36: Now Abigail came to Nabal, and behold, he was holding a feast in his house, like the feast of a king. And Nabal's heart was merry within him, for he was exceedingly drunk; therefore she told him nothing, little or much, until morning light.
verses.25:37: So it came to pass in the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, that his wife told him these things; and his heart died within him, and he became like a stone.
verses.25:38: And it happened, about ten days later, that the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.
verses.25:39: When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Blessed be the LORD, who has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has kept His servant from evil; for the LORD has returned the wickedness of Nabal upon his own head." Then David sent and spoke to Abigail, to take her to himself as a wife.
verses.25:40: When the servants of David came to Abigail at Carmel, they spoke to her, saying, "David has sent us to you, to take you to him as a wife."
verses.25:41: Then she arose, bowed her face to the ground, and said, "Behold, your maidservant is a handmaid to wash the feet of the servants of my lord."
verses.25:42: So Abigail arose in haste and rode on a donkey, attended by five of her young women; and she followed the messengers of David, and became his wife.
verses.25:43: David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel, and so both of them became his wives.
verses.25:44: Now Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti the son of Laish, who was from Gallim.
verses.26:1: Now the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Is David not hiding himself in the hill of Hachilah, facing Jeshimon?"
verses.26:2: Then Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him were three thousand chosen men of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
verses.26:3: And Saul encamped in the hill of Hachilah, which faces Jeshimon, beside the road. But David was dwelling in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness.
verses.26:4: Therefore David sent out spies, and he knew for certain that Saul had come.
verses.26:5: So David arose and came to the place where Saul had encamped. And David saw the place where Saul lay, along with Abner the son of Ner, the commander of his army. Now Saul was lying within the camp enclosure, and the people were encamped all around him.
verses.26:6: Then David answered and spoke to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, "Who will go down with me to Saul into the camp?" And Abishai said, "I will go down with you."
verses.26:7: So David and Abishai came to the people by night; and behold, Saul lay sleeping within the camp enclosure, with his spear thrust into the ground at his head, and Abner and the people were lying all around him.
verses.26:8: Then Abishai said to David, "God has delivered your enemy into your hand this day. Now therefore, let me strike him with the spear straight into the ground at one stroke, and I will not strike him a second time."
verses.26:9: But David said to Abishai, "Do not destroy him; for who can stretch out his hand against the anointed of the LORD and remain guiltless?"
verses.26:10: David also said, "As the LORD lives, surely the LORD shall strike him, or his day shall come to die, or he shall go down into battle and be swept away.
verses.26:11: Far be it from me before the LORD that I should stretch out my hand against the anointed of the LORD! But now, please take the spear that is at his head and the jug of water, and let us go."
verses.26:12: So David took the spear and the jug of water from Saul's head, and they went on their way; and no one saw, and no one knew, and no one awoke, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen upon them.
verses.26:13: Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain at a distance, with a great space between them.
verses.26:14: And David cried out to the people and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, "Will you not answer, Abner?" Then Abner answered and said, "Who are you who calls out to the king?"
verses.26:15: So David said to Abner, "Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? Why then have you not kept watch over your lord the king? For one of the people came in to destroy the king your lord.
verses.26:16: This thing that you have done is not good. As the LORD lives, you are worthy of death, because you have not kept watch over your lord, over the anointed of the LORD. And now see where the king's spear is, and the jug of water that was at his head."
verses.26:17: Then Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" And David said, "It is my voice, my lord the king."
verses.26:18: And he said, "Why does my lord thus pursue after his servant? For what have I done, or what evil is in my hand?
verses.26:19: Now therefore, please let my lord the king hear the words of his servant: If the LORD has incited you against me, let Him accept an offering; but if it is the sons of men, cursed are they before the LORD, for they have driven me out this day from sharing in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, 'Go, serve other gods.'
verses.26:20: Now therefore, do not let my blood fall to the earth away from the presence of the LORD; for the king of Israel has come out to seek a single flea, just as one hunts a partridge in the mountains."
verses.26:21: Then Saul said, "I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will do you harm no more, because my life was precious in your sight this day. Behold, I have acted foolishly and erred exceedingly."
verses.26:22: And David answered and said, "Behold the king's spear! Let one of the young men cross over and fetch it.
verses.26:23: May the LORD repay each man for his righteousness and his faithfulness; for the LORD delivered you into my hand this day, yet I was unwilling to stretch out my hand against the anointed of the LORD.
verses.26:24: And behold, just as your life was highly valued this day in my sight, so let my life be highly valued in the sight of the LORD, and let Him deliver me out of all tribulation."
verses.26:25: Then Saul said to David, "Blessed are you, my son David! You shall both accomplish great things and surely prevail." So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.
verses.27:1: And David said in his heart, "Now I shall perish one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than that I should surely escape into the land of the Philistines; then Saul will despair of seeking me any longer within any territory of Israel, and I shall escape from his hand."
verses.27:2: So David arose and crossed over, he and the six hundred men who were with him, to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
verses.27:3: So David dwelt with Achish at Gath, he and his men, each man with his household, and David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal's widow.
verses.27:4: And it was told to Saul that David had fled to Gath; so he sought him no more.
verses.27:5: Then David said to Achish, "If I have now found favor in your sight, let them give me a place in one of the towns of the open country, that I may dwell there; for why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?"
verses.27:6: So Achish gave him Ziklag that day. Therefore Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this very day.
verses.27:7: Now the length of time that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines was one full year and four months.
verses.27:8: And David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Gizrites, and the Amalekites; for those peoples were from of old the inhabitants of the land, as one goes toward Shur, even to the land of Egypt.
verses.27:9: Whenever David struck the land, he would leave neither man nor woman alive, but he took the sheep, the oxen, the donkeys, the camels, and the apparel, and returned and came to Achish.
verses.27:10: Then Achish would say, "Where did you make a raid today?" And David would say, "Against the Negev of Judah, and against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites, and against the Negev of the Kenites."
verses.27:11: David left neither man nor woman alive to bring to Gath, saying, "Lest they should report against us, saying, 'Thus David has done.'" And such was his custom all the days that he dwelt in the country of the Philistines.
verses.27:12: So Achish trusted David, saying, "He has made himself utterly abhorrent to his people Israel; therefore he shall be my servant forever."
verses.28:1: Now it came to pass in those days that the Philistines gathered their forces together for war, to fight against Israel. And Achish said to David, "Know for certain that you shall go out with me into the camp, you and your men."
verses.28:2: And David said to Achish, "Therefore you yourself shall know what your servant will do." And Achish said to David, "Therefore I will appoint you guardian of my head forever."
verses.28:3: Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had lamented for him and buried him in Ramah, in his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.
verses.28:4: Then the Philistines gathered together and came and encamped at Shunem. So Saul gathered all Israel together, and they encamped at Gilboa.
verses.28:5: When Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart trembled exceedingly.
verses.28:6: And when Saul inquired of the LORD, the LORD did not answer him, either by dreams, or by Urim, or by the prophets.
verses.28:7: Then Saul said to his servants, "Seek out for me a woman who is a medium, that I may go to her and inquire of her." And his servants said to him, "Behold, there is a woman who is a medium at En Dor."
verses.28:8: So Saul disguised himself and put on other garments, and he went, he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night. And he said, "Please divine for me by a familiar spirit, and bring up for me the one whom I shall name to you."
verses.28:9: Then the woman said to him, "Behold, you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why then are you laying a snare for my life, to put me to death?"
verses.28:10: And Saul swore to her by the LORD, saying, "As the LORD lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this thing."
verses.28:11: Then the woman said, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" And he said, "Bring up Samuel for me."
verses.28:12: When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice. And the woman spoke to Saul, saying, "Why have you deceived me? For you are Saul!"
verses.28:13: And the king said to her, "Do not be afraid. What do you see?" And the woman said to Saul, "I saw divine beings ascending out of the earth."
verses.28:14: Then he said to her, "What is his appearance?" And she said, "An old man is ascending, and he is wrapped in a robe." And Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself.
verses.28:15: Now Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" And Saul answered, "I am in great distress; for the Philistines are warring against me, and God has departed from me and answers me no more, neither by the hand of prophets nor by dreams. Therefore I have called for you, that you may make known to me what I shall do."
verses.28:16: Then Samuel said, "Why then do you ask me, seeing the LORD has departed from you and has become your adversary?
verses.28:17: And the LORD has done for Himself just as He spoke by my hand; for the LORD has torn the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David.
verses.28:18: Because you did not obey the voice of the LORD nor execute His fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore the LORD has done this thing to you this day.
verses.28:19: Moreover, the LORD will also deliver Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons shall be with me; the LORD will also deliver the camp of Israel into the hand of the Philistines."
verses.28:20: Immediately Saul fell his full length upon the ground, and was exceedingly afraid because of the words of Samuel; moreover, there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all that day and all that night.
verses.28:21: And the woman came to Saul and saw that he was greatly terrified, and she said to him, "Behold, your maidservant has obeyed your voice, and I have put my life in my hand and have heeded the words which you spoke to me.
verses.28:22: Now therefore, please listen also to the voice of your maidservant, and let me set a morsel of bread before you; and eat, that you may have strength when you go on your way."
verses.28:23: But he refused and said, "I will not eat." Yet his servants, together with the woman, urged him strongly, and he listened to their voice. So he arose from the ground and sat upon the bed.
verses.28:24: Now the woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she hastened to slaughter it; and she took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread from it.
verses.28:25: So she brought it before Saul and before his servants, and they ate. Then they rose up and went away that night.
verses.29:1: Then the Philistines gathered all their camps to Aphek, while Israel was encamped by the spring that is in Jezreel.
verses.29:2: And the lords of the Philistines were passing on by hundreds and by thousands, while David and his men were passing on in the rear with Achish.
verses.29:3: Then the princes of the Philistines said, "What are these Hebrews doing here?" And Achish said to the princes of the Philistines, "Is this not David, the servant of Saul king of Israel, who has been with me these days, or these years? And I have found nothing wrong in him from the day he defected until this day."
verses.29:4: But the princes of the Philistines were angry with him, and the princes of the Philistines said to him, "Send the man back, that he may return to his place where you have appointed him, and do not let him go down with us to the battle, lest he become an adversary to us in the battle. For with what could this man reconcile himself to his master? Would it not be with the heads of those men?
verses.29:5: Is this not David, of whom they sang to one another in the dances, saying, 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
verses.29:6: Then Achish summoned David and said to him, "As the LORD lives, you have been upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in the camp is good in my sight; for I have found no evil in you from the day you came to me until this day. Yet in the sight of the lords you are not favored.
verses.29:7: Therefore now return and go in peace, that you may not do what is evil in the sight of the lords of the Philistines."
verses.29:8: And David said to Achish, "But what have I done? And what have you found in your servant from the day I have been before you until this day, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?"
verses.29:9: Then Achish answered and said to David, "I know that you are as good in my sight as an angel of God; nevertheless, the princes of the Philistines have said, 'He shall not go up with us to the battle.'
verses.29:10: Now therefore rise early in the morning, with the servants of your master who came with you; and as soon as you have risen early in the morning and have light, depart."
verses.29:11: So David rose early, he and his men, to depart in the morning, to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
verses.30:1: Now it came to pass, when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.
verses.30:2: And they had taken captive the women who were in it, both small and great; they did not put anyone to death, but drove them away and went on their way.
verses.30:3: So David and his men came to the city, and behold, it was burned with fire, and their wives, their sons, and their daughters had been taken captive.
verses.30:4: Then David and the people who were with him lifted up their voices and wept, until they had no more strength to weep.
verses.30:5: And David's two wives had been taken captive: Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.30:6: Now David was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was bitter, every man for his sons and for his daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
verses.30:7: Then David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, "Please bring the ephod here to me." And Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
verses.30:8: So David inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I pursue after this raiding band? Shall I overtake them?" And He said to him, "Pursue, for you shall surely overtake them and without fail rescue all."
verses.30:9: So David set out, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the Brook Besor, where those who remained behind stayed.
verses.30:10: But David pursued, he and four hundred men; for two hundred men stayed behind, who were too exhausted to cross the Brook Besor.
verses.30:11: Then they found an Egyptian man in the open field and brought him to David; and they gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.
verses.30:12: And they gave him a slice of a cake of figs and two clusters of raisins; and when he had eaten, his spirit returned to him, for he had eaten no bread nor drunk water for three days and three nights.
verses.30:13: Then David said to him, "To whom do you belong, and where are you from?" And he said, "I am a young Egyptian man, the servant of an Amalekite; and my master abandoned me because three days ago I fell sick.
verses.30:14: We made a raid upon the Negev of the Cherethites, and upon that which belongs to Judah, and upon the Negev of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire."
verses.30:15: And David said to him, "Will you lead me down to this raiding band?" And he said, "Swear to me by God that you will neither put me to death nor deliver me into the hand of my master, and I will lead you down to this raiding band."
verses.30:16: So he led him down, and behold, they were spread out over the face of all the land, eating and drinking and celebrating, because of all the great spoil which they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
verses.30:17: Then David struck them down from twilight until the evening of the next day; and not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men who mounted camels and fled.
verses.30:18: So David rescued all that the Amalekites had taken, and David rescued his two wives.
verses.30:19: And nothing of theirs was missing, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil nor anything that they had taken from them; David brought back everything.
verses.30:20: Then David took all the flocks and the herds, which they drove ahead of the other livestock, and they said, "This is David's spoil."
verses.30:21: Now David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow David, whom they had left to stay at the Brook Besor; and they came out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him. And when David drew near to the people, he inquired after their welfare.
verses.30:22: Then every wicked and worthless man among the men who had gone with David answered and said, "Because they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the spoil which we have recovered, except to every man his wife and his children, that they may lead them away and depart."
verses.30:23: But David said, "You shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the LORD has given us; for He has preserved us and delivered into our hand the raiding band that came against us.
verses.30:24: And who will listen to you in this matter? For as is the share of him who goes down into the battle, so shall be the share of him who stays by the baggage; they shall share alike."
verses.30:25: So it was, from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.
verses.30:26: Now when David came to Ziklag, he sent some of the spoil to the elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, "Behold, a blessing for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD,"
verses.30:27: to those who were in Bethel, to those who were in Ramoth of the Negev, to those who were in Jattir,
verses.30:28: to those who were in Aroer, to those who were in Siphmoth, to those who were in Eshtemoa,
verses.30:29: to those who were in Rachal, to those who were in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, to those who were in the cities of the Kenites,
verses.30:30: to those who were in Hormah, to those who were in Bor-ashan, to those who were in Athach,
verses.30:31: to those who were in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men had roamed.
verses.31:1: Now the Philistines were doing battle against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from the Philistines and fell slain upon Mount Gilboa.
verses.31:2: Then the Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons; and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
verses.31:3: And the battle grew fierce against Saul; and the archers, the men with the bow, found him, and he was severely wounded by the archers.
verses.31:4: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Unsheathe your sword and run me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and run me through and treat me shamefully." Yet his armor-bearer was unwilling, for he was exceedingly afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell upon it.
verses.31:5: Now his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, and he too fell upon his sword and died with him.
verses.31:6: So Saul died, together with his three sons, his armor-bearer, and indeed all his men, on that very day.
verses.31:7: And when the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley and those who were on the other side of the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they forsook the cities and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
verses.31:8: And it came to pass on the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
verses.31:9: Then they cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent word throughout the land of the Philistines round about, to proclaim the tidings in the house of their idols and among the people.
verses.31:10: And they put his armor in the temple of Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.
verses.31:11: Now when the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard concerning him what the Philistines had done to Saul,
verses.31:12: all the valiant men arose and marched all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan; and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.
verses.31:13: Then they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

notes.1:5: The Hebrew phrase rendered "a double portion" is literally "one portion of two faces (appayim)," traditionally understood as a double or especially generous share.
notes.1:16: Hebrew "daughter of Belial" (literally "worthlessness" or "wickedness"), an idiom for a base or wicked person; compare "worthless men" in 2:12.
notes.1:20: Hannah connects the name Samuel with the Hebrew verb shaal ("to ask"), a wordplay continued in 1:27-28 where the same root also conveys "to lend" or "dedicate."
notes.1:24: Translating the Masoretic Hebrew "three bulls" strictly; the Septuagint reads "a three-year-old bull."
notes.2:3: Translating the Masoretic qere ("and by Him"); the written ketiv reads "and not."
notes.2:16: Translating the Masoretic qere ("No"); the written ketiv reads "to him," yielding "then he would say to him, For you shall give it now."
notes.2:25: The Hebrew Elohim may denote "God" or "judges," and the verb palal plays on both the legal sense ("mediate/arbitrate") and the prayerful sense ("intercede").
notes.2:32: The Hebrew phrase tsar maon is difficult and may be rendered either "distress in the habitation" or "an adversary in the habitation."
notes.3:1: The Hebrew word translated rare literally means precious or scarce, and widespread translates a participle meaning breaking forth widely.
notes.3:13: Bringing a curse upon themselves follows the Masoretic Hebrew text; ancient scribal tradition identifies this phrasing as a reverential euphemism avoiding explicit mention of cursing God.
notes.3:19: Let none of his words fall to the ground is a Hebrew idiom meaning that every prophetic word Samuel spoke came to pass.
notes.4:4: Who is enthroned above the cherubim refers to the LORD's symbolic throne above the golden cherubim upon the mercy seat of the ark.
notes.4:13: Beside the road follows the Masoretic Qere reading, meaning at the side of the way, in place of the Ketiv spelling.
notes.4:21: The name Ichabod means Where is the glory or No glory.
notes.5:4: Only the trunk of Dagon was left to him renders the concise Hebrew phrase literally meaning only Dagon remained upon him, referring to the statue's torso.
notes.5:6: Tumors here and in verses nine and twelve follows the Masoretic Qere reading, substituted in public reading for the Ketiv term meaning swellings or boils.
notes.5:10: To us, to slay us and our people, here and similarly in verse eleven, renders a Hebrew corporate singular literally reading to me, to slay me and my people, with Ekron speaking with one voice.
notes.6:4: Here and in verse five, the Qere reads techorim, meaning tumors or growths, whereas the Ketiv reads ophelim, meaning swellings or tumors.
notes.6:18: The Masoretic Hebrew reads Avel haggedolah, rendered Great Abel, whereas verses fourteen and fifteen refer to a large stone, even haggedolah.
notes.6:19: The Masoretic Hebrew places seventy men and fifty thousand men side by side without a conjunction, a famously compressed numerical expression.
notes.7:9: The Qere adds the explicit masculine singular object suffix, reading and offered it, where the Ketiv omits the final letter.
notes.7:12: Ebenezer is Hebrew for Stone of Help, commemorating the LORD's deliverance of Israel.
notes.8:9: The Hebrew word mishpat here denotes the royal practice, custom, or prerogative that a king will exercise over the people.
notes.8:16: The Masoretic Hebrew reads bachureikhem, your young men, translating the Hebrew text directly rather than harmonizing with ancient versions that read cattle.
notes.9:1: Following the Qere, "of Benjamin" is read as a single tribal name, whereas the Ketiv divides it into two words ("from Ben-yamin"). The Hebrew phrase rendered "a mighty man of valor" denotes both personal strength and social standing or wealth.
notes.9:15: "Revealed in Samuel's ear" reflects the Hebrew idiom "uncovered the ear of Samuel," denoting a private disclosure from the LORD.
notes.9:26: Following the Qere, "up to the roof" includes the Hebrew directional ending toward the rooftop, whereas the Ketiv reads simply "the roof."
notes.10:5: "The hill of God" renders Hebrew Gibeat Ha'elohim, a sacred high place associated with the town of Gibeah mentioned in verse 10.
notes.10:7: Following the Qere, the verb "come" uses the standard feminine plural form agreeing with "these signs," while the Ketiv preserves a slight spelling variant.
notes.10:19: The Masoretic Text reads "to Him" (lo) rather than the homophone "no," and "thousands" refers to traditional tribal and military subdivisions of Israel.
notes.10:27: "Worthless men" renders the Hebrew idiom "sons of Belial," meaning base, lawless, or rebellious men.
notes.11:6: Following the Qere, "when he heard" reads the temporal preposition "as/when," whereas the Ketiv reads "in/upon" with essentially the same sense.
notes.11:9: Following the Qere, "by the time the sun grows hot" reads the preposition "about/as," whereas the Ketiv reads "in the heat of the sun."
notes.11:14: "Renew the kingdom" signifies a solemn public confirmation of Saul's kingship before the LORD following his victory at Jabesh Gilead.
notes.12:10: The written text (ketiv) has the singular verb "he said," while the read text (qere), translated here, has the plural "they said."
notes.12:11: "Bedan" follows the Masoretic Hebrew text; some ancient versions read "Barak," while Jewish tradition often identifies Bedan with Samson ("of Dan").
notes.12:15: The Hebrew literally reads "against you and against your fathers," often understood comparatively as "against you, just as it was against your fathers."
notes.12:21: The Hebrew term for "vain things" and "vanity" (tohu) denotes emptiness and nothingness, highlighting the complete futility of idols.
notes.13:8: The written text (ketiv) and read text (qere) differ slightly in the vocalization and spelling of the verb "waited," with the qere followed here.
notes.13:19: The written text (ketiv) has the singular verb "said," while the read text (qere), followed here, has the plural verb agreeing with "the Philistines."
notes.13:20: The first and fourth agricultural tools share closely related Hebrew forms of the same root, traditionally rendered as two distinct iron implements such as a plowshare and a sickle.
notes.13:21: A "pim" was an ancient weight equal to about two-thirds of a shekel of silver, attested by inscribed stone weights recovered in archaeological excavations.
notes.14:14: The Hebrew expression translated "half a furrow of a yoke of field" refers to a small plot of ground, roughly half an acre, measured by what a yoke of oxen could plow.
notes.14:27: Following the Masoretic Qere "brightened" (restored in strength and vitality); the Ketiv reads "saw."
notes.14:32: Following the Masoretic Qere "rushed" and "the spoil"; the Ketiv reads "acted" (or "made") and "spoil" without the definite article.
notes.14:41: The phrase "Give a true lot" translates the concise Masoretic Hebrew literally reading "Give perfection," a solemn petition for an unerring verdict by lot.
notes.15:11: The Hebrew verb nacham ("regret" in 15:11, 35; "relent" in 15:29) expresses both divine sorrow over human disobedience and the reversal of a decree, contrasting God's grief over Saul with His unchanging purpose.
notes.15:16: The Masoretic ketiv reads the plural "they said," whereas the qere (translated here) reads the singular "he said," referring directly to Saul.
notes.15:23: The term translated "idolatry" is Hebrew teraphim, denoting household idols associated with pagan worship and divination.
notes.15:32: The rare Hebrew adverb ma'adannot ("cheerfully") derives from a root denoting ease or delight, indicating that Agag approached Samuel with confident relief.
notes.16:7: The expression "to the outward appearance" literally reads "to the eyes" in Hebrew, contrasting human judgment based on what is visible with the LORD's discernment of the heart.
notes.16:11: The Hebrew verb nasov ("sit down") literally means "turn around" or "recline in a circle," referring to gathering around the sacrificial feast.
notes.16:14: The Hebrew phrase ruach ra'ah ("an evil spirit") refers to a distressing or injurious spirit operating under the LORD's sovereign permission.
notes.16:20: The Hebrew literally reads "a donkey of bread," an idiomatic expression for a donkey laden with loaves of bread.
notes.17:4: Hebrew ish-habbenayim literally means a man of the space between, denoting a single-combat champion who stepped out between two opposing battle lines.
notes.17:7: The Masoretic Qere reads the wood or shaft of his spear, which is translated here, whereas the Ketiv reads the arrow or point of his spear.
notes.17:52: The Masoretic text reads the entrance to the valley, Hebrew Gai, as the initial boundary of the pursuit.
notes.18:6: The Masoretic Qere reads to sing, translated here, while the Ketiv preserves an alternate spelling of the verb. The Hebrew term shalishim denotes a musical instrument, likely three-stringed or triangular, whose exact form is uncertain.
notes.18:9: The Masoretic Qere reads oyein, a participle derived from the word for eye meaning to watch with jealousy or suspicion, whereas the Ketiv writes a shorter consonantal form.
notes.18:14: The Hebrew participle maskil conveys both acting with prudent wisdom and enjoying consequent success.
notes.19:13: The Hebrew teraphim is plural in form yet refers here to a single household image or statue; "quilt of goats' hair" renders a rare Hebrew expression for a woven mat or pillow of goat hair.
notes.19:18: The qere reads "in Naioth" (and likewise in 19:19, 19:22, 19:23, and "from Naioth" in 20:1), denoting the prophetic settlement at Ramah, whereas the ketiv preserves an older orthographic form of the same name.
notes.19:20: "Company of the prophets" translates a rare Hebrew term (lahakah) denoting a prophetic band assembled under Samuel's leadership.
notes.20:2: The qere reads the negative particle with the imperfect verb ("does nothing"), whereas the ketiv displays an older spelling of the negative with a perfect verb.
notes.20:14: The Masoretic Hebrew employs compressed negative syntax connecting Jonathan's request for covenantal lovingkindness during his own lifetime with its continuance to his house in verse fifteen.
notes.20:24: The qere reads the preposition "to" ("to the meal"), while the ketiv reads the closely related preposition "at" or "upon."
notes.20:38: The qere reads the plural "the arrows," matching verses twenty and thirty-six, whereas the ketiv reads the singular "the arrow," matching verses thirty-six and thirty-seven.
notes.20:41: "From the south side" faithfully renders the Masoretic Hebrew expression meaning "from beside the south."
notes.21:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification, chapter 21 begins with this verse (numbered 20:42b in many English translations), shifting all subsequent verse numbers in chapter 21 by one.
notes.21:6: The Hebrew phrase rendered 'vessels' (keli) may refer to the young men's gear or figuratively to their bodies; the closing clause is compressed in Hebrew and indicates that their ritual purity is all the more certain on the present occasion.
notes.21:7: Literally 'bread of the face' (showbread), the twelve consecrated loaves regularly replaced before the LORD (Leviticus 24:5–9).
notes.22:6: Hebrew ba-ramah can be read either as 'on the height' at Gibeah or as the town name 'in Ramah.'
notes.22:15: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv reads the plene spelling lish'ol and the Qere reads lish'al ('to inquire'), with identical meaning.
notes.22:17: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv reads 'his ear' (ozno), while the Qere followed here reads 'my ear' (ozni), using the Hebrew idiom 'uncover the ear' for informing someone.
notes.22:18: Ketiv/Qere: here and in verse 22 the Ketiv spells the name Doyeg, while the Qere followed here reads Doeg (as in 21:8 and 22:9).
notes.23:15: Horesh (Hebrew horeshah) denotes a wooded area or forest site within the Wilderness of Ziph.
notes.23:19: Jeshimon means 'the wasteland' or 'the desert,' referring to the barren wilderness overlooking the Dead Sea; Hebrew 'on the right hand' indicates the south when facing east.
notes.23:28: Hebrew Sela Hammahlekoth, literally 'Rock of Divisions' or 'Rock of Slipping Away' (often understood as 'Rock of Escape'), commemorating how Saul and David were parted there.
notes.24:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification followed here, 24:1 corresponds to 23:29 in many English Bibles, and the remaining verses of the chapter are numbered one verse higher.
notes.24:4: The Hebrew idiom 'to cover his feet' is a modest euphemism for relieving oneself.
notes.24:5: The Masoretic qere (read form) is singular, 'your enemy,' whereas the ketiv (written form) is plural, 'your enemies.'
notes.24:11: The verb rendered 'I spared you' is literally feminine singular ('it spared you'), an idiomatic ellipsis for 'my eye spared you.'
notes.24:19: Following the Masoretic qere 'and you' (ve'attah); the ketiv reads the shorter form ve'at. Similarly, in 24:9 the qere contracts 'from the cave' into a single word.
notes.25:3: Following the Masoretic qere 'a Calebite' (a descendant of Caleb); the ketiv spelling reads literally 'like his heart,' a wordplay on Nabal's stubborn character.
notes.25:6: The terse Hebrew greeting literally means 'thus to life' or 'thus to him who lives,' expressing a wish for enduring life and prosperity.
notes.25:18: Both 'Abigail' and 'dressed' (prepared) follow the Masoretic qere spellings over the ketiv forms. A seah was a dry measure of roughly seven liters.
notes.25:22: The Masoretic text reads 'to the enemies of David,' a traditional reverent euphemism avoiding a direct self-curse upon David. The phrase rendered 'a single male' translates a blunt Hebrew idiom (also in 25:34) meaning literally 'one who urinates against a wall.'
notes.25:34: The verb 'and come' follows the Masoretic qere spelling over the longer ketiv form.
notes.26:16: Literally "sons of death," a Hebrew idiom meaning deserving of capital punishment.
notes.26:19: Literally "let Him smell an offering," an anthropomorphic idiom for God favorably accepting a sacrifice.
notes.26:22: Ketiv/Qere: the written text reads "the spear" with the definite article, while the traditional reading (Qere) follows the construct form "the king's spear."
notes.27:4: Ketiv/Qere: the written text has an imperfect verb form, whereas the traditional reading (Qere) reads the perfect form, both meaning that Saul ceased pursuing David.
notes.27:7: Literally "days and four months"; in biblical Hebrew, "days" often serves idiomatically for a full year.
notes.27:8: Ketiv/Qere: the written text reads "the Girzites," while the traditional reading (Qere) reads "the Gizrites."
notes.27:10: The Masoretic Text has the unusual interrogative particle al, understood idiomatically here as an elliptical question asking where David raided.
notes.28:8: Ketiv/Qere: the written text spells the feminine singular imperative "divine" with a medial vav, while the traditional reading (Qere) vocalizes the standard imperative form.
notes.28:13: Hebrew elohim is construed here with a plural participle to denote a supernatural or ghostly apparition, though Saul refers to the figure in the singular in verse 14.
notes.28:17: The Masoretic Text reads "for Himself," emphasizing that the LORD acted on His own behalf to fulfill what He had spoken through Samuel.
notes.29:4: The Hebrew term rendered adversary is satan, used here in its ordinary sense of a military opponent or traitor within the ranks.
notes.29:6: The title lords translates the distinctive Philistine loanword seranim, designating the rulers of the five major Philistine cities, as distinguished from the military princes or commanders in verses 3, 4, and 9.
notes.30:1: The Negev refers to the arid southern steppe region extending south of the hill country of Judah.
notes.30:20: The concise Hebrew clause literally reads, they drove before that livestock, indicating that David's men drove the newly captured Amalekite flocks and herds ahead of their own recovered livestock as David's special portion of the spoil.
notes.30:22: The Masoretic Text reads with me in the singular, aligning with the distributive subject every wicked and worthless man, before shifting to the plural we will not give.
notes.30:30: Bor-ashan follows the Masoretic Hebrew literally, meaning Cistern of Smoke, a town in southern Judah associated with the territory of Simeon.
notes.31:3: The Hebrew verb rendered severely wounded may alternatively be derived from a root meaning to writhe or tremble in terror before the archers.
notes.31:10: Ashtaroth is plural in Hebrew, referring to the temple dedicated to the Canaanite and Philistine fertility goddess Ashtoreth and her cultic images.
notes.31:13: The tamarisk tree translates the Hebrew eshel, a hardy desert evergreen often marking notable landmarks and memorial burial sites in ancient Israel.
